title: Purpose: refund of ancillary service fees not provided
text: The purpose of this part is to ensure that carriers promptly refund consumers for: (a) Fees for ancillary services related to air travel that consumers paid for but were not provided;
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Purpose: refund of lost or significantly delayed checked bag fees

source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Purpose: refund of airfare for cancelled or significantly changed flights
text: (c) Airfare including nonrefundable airfare for a flight that is cancelled or significantly changed where the consumer does not accept the significantly changed flight or rebooking on an alternative flight, or accept any voucher, credit, or other compensation offered by the carrier.

title: Definition: ancillary service
text: Ancillary service means any optional service related to air travel that a covered carrier provides for a fee, beyond passenger air transportation. Such services may include, but are not limited to, transport of checked or carry-on baggage, advance seat selection, access to in-flight entertainment programs or Wi-Fi, in-flight beverages, snacks, meals, pillows and blankets, seat upgrades, and lounge access.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)
ambiguity_note: Services listed with 'may include, but are not limited to' so the full set of covered services is open-ended.

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Definition: automatic refund
text: Automatic refund means issuing a refund to a consumer without waiting to receive an explicit refund request, when the consumer's right to a refund is undisputed because the contracted service was not provided and either the consumer rejected the alternative offered or no alternative was offered.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Definition: cancelled flight
text: Cancelled flight or flight cancellation means a covered flight with a specific flight number scheduled to be operated between a specific origin-destination city pair that was published in the carrier's Computer Reservation System at the time of the ticket sale but not operated by the carrier.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Definition: cash equivalent
text: Cash equivalent means a form of payment that can be used like cash, including but not limited to a check, a prepaid card, funds transferred to a consumer's bank account, funds provided through digital payment methods (e.g., PayPal, Venmo), or a gift card that is widely accepted in commerce. It is not cash equivalent if consumers bear the burden for transaction, maintenance, or usage fees related to the payment.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)
ambiguity_note: 'Widely accepted in commerce' for gift cards is not quantified.

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Definition: checked bag
text: Checked bag means a bag, special item (e.g., musical instrument or a pet), or sports equipment (e.g., golf clubs) that was provided to a covered carrier by or on behalf of a passenger for transportation in the cargo compartment of a scheduled passenger flight. A checked bag includes a gate-checked bag and a valet bag.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Definition: significantly delayed or changed flight
text: Significantly delayed or changed flight means a covered flight itinerary with a delay or change made by a covered carrier where, as the result of the delay or change: (1) The consumer is scheduled to depart from the origination airport three hours or more for domestic itineraries and six hours or more for international itineraries earlier than the original scheduled departure time;
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Significant change: arrival time shift
text: (2) The consumer is scheduled to arrive at the destination airport three or more hours for domestic itineraries or six or more hours for international itineraries after the original scheduled arrival time;
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Significant change: different airports
text: (3) The consumer is scheduled to depart from a different origination airport or arrive at a different destination airport;
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Significant change: additional connections
text: (4) The consumer is scheduled to travel on an itinerary with more connection points than that of the original itinerary;
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Significant change: downgrade
text: (5) The consumer is downgraded to a lower class of service;
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Significant change: disability connecting airports
text: (6) The consumer who is an individual with a disability is scheduled to travel through one or more connecting airports different from the original itinerary; or
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Significant change: disability substitute aircraft
text: (7) The consumer who is an individual with a disability is scheduled to travel on substitute aircraft on which one or more accessibility features needed by the customer are unavailable.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Definition: significantly delayed checked bag
text: Significantly delayed checked bag means a checked bag not delivered to or picked up by the consumer or another person authorized to act on behalf of the consumer within 12 hours of the last flight segment's arrival for domestic itineraries, within 15 hours of the last flight segment's arrival for international itineraries with a non-stop flight segment between the United States and a foreign point that is 12 hours or less in duration, and within 30 hours of the last flight segment's arrival for international itineraries with a non-stop flight segment between the United States and a foreign point that is more than 12 hours in duration.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Applicability: merchant of record and ticket agents
text: This part applies to: covered carriers that are the merchants of record; covered carriers that operate the flight or, for multiple-carrier itineraries, covered carriers that operate the last segment of a flight where a ticket agent is the merchant of record for a checked bag fee; and covered carriers that fail to provide an ancillary service (other than checked bag service) for which the consumer paid where a ticket agent is the merchant of record for an ancillary service fee other than checked bag fee.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Automatic refund of ancillary fees for services not provided (merchant of record carrier)
text: A covered carrier that is the merchant of record shall provide a prompt and automatic refund to a consumer for any fees it collected from the consumer for ancillary services if the service was not provided through no fault of the consumer
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Checked bag fee refund when ticket agent is merchant of record
text: If a ticket agent is the merchant of record for a checked bag fee and the checked bag service was not provided (or was significantly delayed) through no fault of the consumer, the carrier that operated the flight, or for multiple-carrier itineraries, the carrier that operated the last segment of the consumer's itinerary is responsible for providing a prompt and automatic refund of the checked bag fee, consistent with § 260.5.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund of other ancillary fees when ticket agent is merchant of record
text: If a ticket agent is the merchant of record for fees for all other ancillary services, the carrier that operated the flight and failed to provide the service through no fault of the consumer is responsible for providing a prompt and automatic refund.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund start when service unavailable for all passengers
text: In situations where the ancillary service the consumer paid for (other than the service of transporting a checked bag) is not available for all the passengers who paid for that service (e.g., Wi-Fi not available for all passengers on a flight, lounge access not available for all passengers on a certain date), a carrier's obligation under paragraph (a) of this section to provide a prompt and automatic refund begins when the information about the unavailability of the service is known by the carrier that failed to provide the service
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund start when service unavailable to individual passengers
text: a carrier's obligation under paragraph (a) of this section to provide a prompt and automatic refund begins when the consumer affected by the service failure notifies the operating carrier that failed to provide the ancillary service about the unavailability of the service and that information has been confirmed
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Consumer notification treated as refund request
text: Notification of the unavailability of the ancillary service by a consumer is considered a request for a refund.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Operating carrier must timely notify merchant of record carrier
text: the operating carrier that failed to provide the ancillary service must timely notify the carrier that is the merchant of record about the unavailability of the ancillary service. Notification by the operating carrier as set forth in this paragraph is necessary for the obligation to provide a prompt refund of ancillary service fees in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section to apply.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)
ambiguity_note: 'Timely' is not defined by a number of days.

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund of lost or significantly delayed bag fee
text: A covered carrier that is the merchant of record or, if a ticket agent is the merchant of record, the covered carrier that operated the flight or the last flight segment in a multiple-carrier itinerary, must provide a prompt refund to a consumer of any fee charged for transporting a lost bag or a significantly delayed checked bag
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Length of bag delay measurement
text: the length of delay is calculated from the time the passenger is given the opportunity to deplane from a flight at the passenger's final destination airport (the beginning of the delay) to the time that the carrier has delivered the bag to a location agreed upon by the passenger and carrier (e.g., passenger's home or hotel) or the time that the bag has been picked up by the passenger or another person acting on behalf of the passenger at the passenger's final destination airport (the end of the delay).
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Mishandled Baggage Report required for bag fee refund
text: A covered carrier does not have an obligation to provide a refund of the fee for a lost or significantly delayed checked bag unless a passenger files a Mishandled Baggage Report (MBR) for the lost or delayed bag with the carrier that operated the flight, or for multiple-carrier itineraries, the carrier that operated the last segment of the consumer's itinerary.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Carrier receiving MBR must timely notify refund carrier
text: Except when the carrier responsible for providing a prompt refund for a baggage fee as specified in this section is the same carrier that received the MBR, a covered carrier that received the MBR must timely notify the carrier responsible for providing a prompt refund that the bag has been lost or significantly delayed when this is the case.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)
ambiguity_note: 'Timely' is not defined by a number of days.

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Automatic bag fee refund conditions
text: An automatic refund of a bag fee is due when a checked bag is significantly delayed as determined according to paragraph (a) of this section, the passenger has filed an MBR as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, and, if applicable, notification has been provided by the carrier that received the MBR as set forth in paragraph (c) of this section.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund amount for checked bag fee
text: The amount of the refund issued to a consumer must be a value equal to or greater than the fee that the consumer paid to transport his/her checked bag.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund amount for escalated multiple bag fee scale
text: For carriers that adopt an escalated baggage fee scale for multiple bags checked by one passenger, the amount of baggage fee refund issued to the passenger can be determined based on the unique identifier assigned to the significantly delayed or lost bag that correlates to the baggage fee charged for that bag at the time of checking. If there is no such unique identifier assigned, carriers must refund the highest per bag fee or fees charged for the multiple bags.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund amount for baggage fee subscription
text: For a carrier that offers a baggage fee subscription program where consumers can pay a subscription fee that covers fees for checked bags for a specified period, the carrier must refund the lowest amount of the baggage fee the carrier charges another passenger of similar frequent flyer status and in the same class of service without the subscription when a passenger subscribing to the program has a significantly delayed or lost bag.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Exemption for failure to recheck bag at US international entry
text: A passenger's failure to pick up and recheck a bag at the first international entry point into the United States as required by U.S. Customs and Border Protection;
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Exemption for passenger fault in bag pickup
text: A passenger's failure to pick up a checked bag that arrived on time at the passenger's ticketed final destination due to the fault of the passenger if documented by the carrier (e.g., passenger ended the travel before reaching the final destination on the itinerary—“hidden city” itinerary, or the passenger failed to pick up the bag before taking a flight on a separate itinerary)
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Exemption for voluntary agreement to travel without bag
text: A passenger's voluntary agreement to travel without the checked bag on the same flight as described in paragraph (g) of this section.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Carrier may require new bag delivery agreement for late check-in or standby
text: A carrier may require a passenger who fails to meet the minimum check-in time requirement for a flight or is a standby passenger for a flight (i.e., a passenger who lacks a reservation on that flight and is waiting at the gate for a seat to be available on the flight) to agree to a new baggage delivery date and location in situations where the carrier is unable to place the passenger's checked bag on that flight because of the limited time available.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: No waiver of bag fee refund, compensation or expense rights
text: The carrier must not require the passenger to waive the right to a refund of bag fees if the bag is lost, the right to compensation for damaged, lost, or pilfered bags, or the right to incidental expenses reimbursement arising from delayed bags beyond the agreed upon delivery date, consistent with the Department's regulation in 14 CFR part 254 and applicable international treaties.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Carrier obligation to refund cancelled or significantly changed flight
text: A covered carrier that is the merchant of record must provide a full and prompt refund of the airfare, including any taxes and ancillary fees, as set forth in paragraph (a)(2) of this section to a consumer that holds a nonrefundable ticket on a scheduled flight to, from, or within the United States for any cancelled flight or significantly delayed or changed flight where the consumer chooses not to:
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)
ambiguity_note: 'Significantly delayed or changed' is not quantified in this chunk; the threshold is defined elsewhere in the part.

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund if consumer declines flight or rebooking
text: (i) Fly on the significantly delayed or changed flight or accept rebooking on an alternative flight;
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund if consumer declines voucher or compensation
text: (ii) Accept any voucher, credit, or other form of compensation offered by the air carrier or foreign air carrier pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Automatic refund on cancelled flight without alternative
text: (i) A flight is canceled and a consumer is not offered an alternative flight or any voucher, credit, or other form of compensation by the air carrier or foreign air carrier pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section;
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Automatic refund on rejection of delayed, changed, rebooked or compensated travel
text: (ii) A consumer rejects the significantly delayed or changed flight, rebooking on an alternative flight, or any voucher, credit, or other form of compensation offered by the covered carrier pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section; or
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Automatic refund on no response to offer, flight departs without consumer
text: (A) A significantly delayed or changed flight or an alternative flight and the flight departs without the consumer; or
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Automatic refund on no response to compensation offer by deadline
text: (B) A voucher, credit, or other form of compensation by the date on which the cancelled flight was scheduled to depart or the date that the significantly delayed or changed flight departs.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund for individuals with a disability on significant changes
text: A carrier that is the merchant of record must provide a full and prompt refund to an individual with a disability upon notification by the individual with a disability that he/she does not want to continue travel because of the significant changes described in paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Refund to others in reservation of disabled passenger
text: The covered carrier must also provide a full and prompt refund to any individuals in the same reservation as the individual with a disability who do not want to continue travel without the individual with a disability in situations described in paragraphs (b)(1) through (3).
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Downgrade making accessibility features unavailable
text: (1) The individual with a disability is downgraded to a lower class of service that results in one or more accessibility features needed by the individual becoming unavailable.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Connecting airport change affecting disabled passenger
text: (2) The individual with a disability is scheduled to travel through one or more connecting airports that are different from the original itinerary.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Substitute aircraft lacking accessibility features
text: (3) The individual with a disability is scheduled to travel on a substitute aircraft on which one or more accessibility features available on the original aircraft needed by the individual are unavailable.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Conditions for alternative voucher in lieu of refund
text: A covered carrier may offer a voucher, credit, or other form of compensation as an explicit alternative to providing a refund required by paragraph (a) of this section if:
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Clear notice of alternative terms and refund right
text: (1) The offer includes a clear and conspicuous notice of— (i) The terms of the offer as specified in § 260.8; and (ii) The consumer's right to a full refund under this section.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Five-year validity of voucher in lieu of refund
text: The voucher, credit, or other form of compensation offered explicitly as an alternative to providing a refund required by paragraph (a) of this section remains valid and redeemable by the consumer for a period of at least five years from the date on which such voucher, credit, or other form of compensation is issued;
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Notice of voucher expiration date
text: Upon the issuance of such voucher, credit, or other form of compensation, a covered carrier notifies the recipient of the expiration date of the voucher, credit, or other form of compensation; and
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Accessible expiration notice on request
text: Upon request by an individual who self identifies as an individual with a disability a covered carrier provides a notification under paragraph (c)(3) of this section in an electronic format accessible to the recipient.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Carrier must inform ticket agent of refund eligibility
text: In situations where a ticket agent is the merchant of record for the transaction, after receiving a refund request by a consumer through the ticket agent, the carrier that canceled or significantly delayed or changed the flight must inform the ticket agent without delay whether the consumer is eligible for a refund under this section
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Carrier must transfer funds to ticket agent
text: In situations where a ticket agent is responsible for providing the refund to the consumer pursuant to 14 CFR 399.80(l) and the ticket agent does not possess the funds of the consumer, that carrier that has the funds must promptly transfer the funds to the ticket agent.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: No deemed acceptance of compensation without affirmative agreement
text: A covered carrier must not deem a consumer to have accepted an offer for travel credits, vouchers, or other compensation in lieu of a refund under § 260.6(c) unless the consumer affirmatively agrees to the alternative form of compensation.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Disclosure of material restrictions on vouchers
text: In carrying out the requirements of § 260.6(c), a covered carrier must clearly and conspicuously disclose, no later than at the time of voucher or credit offer, any material restrictions, limitations, or conditions on travel credits, vouchers, or other compensation, including but not limited to validity period, advance purchase requirement, capacity restrictions, and blackout dates, regardless of whether consumers are entitled to a refund.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Timely notice of cancellation or significant change
text: Upon the occurrence of a flight cancellation or a significant delay or change, a covered carrier must timely notify affected consumers about the cancellation or significant delay or change, and the information relating to any alternative to refund as provided in § 260.6(c).
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)
ambiguity_note: 'Timely' is not defined with a number of days.

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Notice of right to refund through passenger notification systems
text: Covered air carriers must ensure that their passenger notification systems notify passengers owed a refund pursuant to § 260.6(a) and (b) of their right to receive a refund.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Notification through subscriber-chosen media
text: Covered carriers that provide notification subscription services to passengers must ensure notifications under this paragraph be provided through media that the carriers offer and the subscribers choose, including emails, text messages, and push notices from mobile apps.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Prompt refund in original form of payment
text: When a refund of a fare or a fee for an ancillary service, including a fee for lost or significantly delayed checked baggage, is due pursuant to this part, the refund must be issued promptly in the original form of payment (i.e., money is returned to an individual using whatever payment method the individual used to make the original payment, such as a check, credit card, debit card, cash, or airline miles) unless the consumer agrees to receive the refunds in a different form of payment that is a cash equivalent as defined in § 260.2.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

provenance.document_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: No processing fee on refunds
text: Carriers may not retain a processing fee for issuing refunds that are due.
source_title: 14 CFR Part 260 - Refunds for airline fare and ancillary service fees (US DOT)

title: Contract of carriage must not conflict with refund rules
text: A carrier must not include terms or conditions in its contract of carriage inconsistent with the carriers' obligations as specified by this part. Any such action will be considered an unfair and deceptive practice within the meaning of 49 U.S.C. 41712.

title: Credit validity
text: A Credit must be used for travel booked and flown within one (1) year from date of issuance. Credits are non-transferable unless otherwise stated herein.

title: Credit definition
text: Credit means a Credit in a specified dollar amount valid for one (1) year from the date of issuance.

title: Force majeure definition
text: Force Majeure Event means any event outside Carrier's control, which includes, but is not limited to, weather conditions and meteorological events, such as storms, rain, wind, fire, fog, flooding, earthquakes, haze, or volcanic eruption; acts of government or airport authorities (e.g., air traffic control delays, runway closures, airport construction); acts of God; pandemics, quarantines, U.S. military or airlift emergency or substantially expanded U.S. military airlift requirements, as determined by the U.S. government; grounding of a substantial number of aircraft as a result of activation of the U.S. Civil Reserve Air Fleet; strikes, work stoppages, slowdowns, lockouts or any other labor unrest or disputes involving or affecting Carrier's service; civil commotions, disturbances or potentially volatile conditions, riots, embargoes, wars or other hostilities, whether actual, threatened or reported; government regulation, demand or requirement; damage to aircraft caused by a third party; mechanical difficulties by entities other than Alaska; inability to obtain fuel, airport gates, labor or landing facilities for the flight in question; an emergency situation requiring care, protection or response to protect persons or property; or any event that is not reasonably foreseen, predicted or anticipated by Carrier.
ambiguity_note: Broad list; 'any event that is not reasonably foreseen' is open-ended and leaves outcome to carrier judgment.

title: Baggage definition
text: Baggage means all luggage and contents contained therein, such as articles, effects and other personal property of a ticketed Passenger as are reasonably necessary or appropriate for the wear, use, comfort or convenience of the Passenger in connection with the Passenger's trip.
ambiguity_note: 'reasonably necessary or appropriate' is a subjective standard.

title: Coats excluded from baggage
text: Coats and wraps, when carried by the Passenger in the Passenger cabin, will not be considered as Baggage.

title: Checked baggage definition
text: Checked Baggage means Baggage that a ticketed Passenger has requested be carried by the Carrier and for which the Carrier has issued a Baggage Claim Tag to the Passenger.

title: Carry-on baggage definition
text: Carry-On Bag or Carry-On Baggage means Baggage, other than Checked Baggage, carried on board an aircraft by a ticketed Passenger, and is also known as Unchecked Baggage, including but not limited to roller bags, duffle bags, backpacks, and garment bags, as long as by its dimensions or nature does not diminish the comfort and safety of the aircraft passengers.
ambiguity_note: Carrier judgment of 'comfort and safety' determines whether an item qualifies.

title: Cabin-seat baggage definition
text: Cabin-Seat Baggage means Carry-On Baggage that due to its size and nature requires the purchase of a seat on board the aircraft to transport the piece of Baggage.

title: Consequential damages definition
text: Consequential Damages means damages which are the result of an act but are not direct or immediate.

title: Contract amendment
text: Contract of Carriage means the terms and conditions contained in this document, as it may be amended from time to time by Alaska.

title: Governing law precedence
text: This Contract of Carriage is subject to Applicable Laws, regulations and rules imposed by U.S. and foreign governmental agencies. In the event of a conflict between the terms of this Contract of Carriage and such Applicable Laws, regulations or rules, the latter shall apply.

title: Terms binding on purchase
text: By purchasing a Ticket or accepting Domestic Carriage or International Carriage on Alaska and/or Alaska's regional partners or Codeshare Partners, the Passenger agrees to be bound by all of the terms and conditions of this Contract of Carriage, and no covenants at law or in equity shall be implied or incorporated.

title: Circle trip stopover limit
text: No more than two (2) Stopovers may be made in the fare construction.

title: Adult definition
text: Adult means a person who has reached his/her eighteenth birthday as of the date of commencement of travel.

title: Child definition
text: Child means a person who has reached his/her second birthday but not his/her 12th birthday as of the date of commencement of travel.

title: Domestic carriage definition
text: Domestic Carriage or Domestic Air Transportation ("Domestic") means transportation in which the place of departure, the place of Destination or Stopover, and the entire transportation is between points within the United States.

title: Schedule Irregularity definition
text: RR. Schedule Irregularity means any of the following, unless due to a Force Majeure Event: a. Delay in scheduled departure or arrival of flight resulting in a misconnection; or b. Flight or service cancellation, omission of a scheduled stop, or any other delay or interruption exceeding 180 minutes of the scheduled operation of an Alaska flight; or c. Substitution of aircraft type that provides a different class of service; or d. Schedule Changes which require rerouting of the Passenger at departure time of the original flight.

title: Significantly delayed or Changed Flight definition
text: XX. Significantly delayed or Changed Flight means any of the following a. The guest is scheduled to depart from the origination airport three or more hours earlier or later than the original departure time. b. The guest is scheduled to arrive at the destination airport three or more hours earlier or later than the original arrival time. c. The guest is scheduled to depart from a different origination airport or arrive at a different destination airport. d. The guest is downgraded to a lower class of service. e. The guest is scheduled to travel on an itinerary with more connection points than the original itinerary; or f. The guest with a disability is scheduled to travel through one or more connecting airports that are different from the original itinerary. g. The guest with a disability is scheduled to travel on a substitute aircraft on which one or more accessibility features needed by them are unavailable.

title: Oversold Flight definition
text: MM. Oversold Flight means a flight where there are more Passengers holding valid confirmed reservations and Tickets that check-in for the flight within the prescribed check-in time than there are available seats.

title: Stopover definition
text: AAA. Stopover means a deliberate or intentional interruption of a journey by a Passenger, agreed to in advance by Alaska, scheduled to exceed four (4) hours at a point between the place of departure and the place of destination for travel within the United States or between the United States and Canada, or twenty-four (24) hours otherwise.

title: Unaccompanied Minor definition
text: FFF. Unaccompanied Minor means a Child/Minor of 5 to 17 years of age when traveling alone or not accompanied on the same flight and in the same compartment by a companion Passenger of at least 18 years of age or with a legal guardian or parent.

title: Service Animal definition
text: WW. Service Animal means a dog, regardless of breed or type, that is individually trained to do work or perform tasks for the benefit of a Qualified Individual With a Disability, including a visual, sensory, psychiatric, intellectual, or other mental disability. Animal species other than dogs, emotional support animals, comfort animals, companionship animals, and service animals in training are not Service Animals.

title: Unchecked Baggage definition
text: GGG. Unchecked Baggage means Baggage, other than Checked Baggage, carried on board an aircraft by a ticketed Passenger, and is also known as Carry-On Baggage.

title: Most Significant Carrier baggage rules
text: The selecting Carrier is permitted to use the MSC to determine which Carrier's Baggage rules apply to an international Interline itinerary to or from Canada, while reinforcing the role of tariffs in the determination of which Carrier's rules apply.
ambiguity_note: Uses 'permitted to' rather than a firm rule; which carrier's baggage rules apply is left to the selecting carrier.

title: Definition of denied boarding (EU/UK)
text: Denied boarding means a refusal to carry passengers on a flight, although they have presented themselves for boarding under the conditions laid down in Article 3(2), except where there are reasonable grounds to deny them boarding, such as reasons of health, safety or security, or inadequate travel documentation.

title: Definition of final destination (EU/UK)
text: Final destination means the destination on the ticket presented at the check-in counter or, in the case of directly connecting flights, the destination of the last flight; alternative connecting flights available shall not be taken into account if the original planned arrival time is respected

title: Alaska cancellation for government, defense or force majeure
text: Alaska reserves the right to cancel a reservation (whether or not confirmed) and seat assignment of any Passenger whenever necessary to comply with any governmental regulation or request for emergency transportation in connection with the national defense, or whenever necessary or advisable by reason of a Force Majeure Event.
ambiguity_note: Right to cancel is discretionary ('reserves the right'); 'necessary or advisable' is not objectively defined.

title: Refund on cancellation of reservations for airports awaiting approval
text: For reservations on flights to/from airports for which Alaska is awaiting regulatory or governmental approval to operate, Alaska reserves the right to cancel a reservation and issue a refund to Passengers.
ambiguity_note: Cancellation and refund are at Alaska's discretion ('reserves the right'); no timing or amount specified.

provenance.section: Rule 7. Cancellation of Reservations and Prohibited Practices

title: Cancellation for passenger non-compliance or non-payment
text: Alaska reserves the right to cancel a reservation (whether or not confirmed) due to the Passenger's failure to comply with the rules set forth in this Contract of Carriage, including, but not limited to, the Passenger's failure to pay for the applicable Ticket under the conditions applicable to the fare for such travel.
ambiguity_note: Discretionary right to cancel; 'including, but not limited to' leaves scope open.

provenance.section: Rule 7. Cancellation of Reservations and Prohibited Practices

title: Failure to occupy reserved space (no-show)
text: If a Passenger fails to occupy space which has been reserved for him/her on a flight and Alaska does not receive notice of cancellation of the reservation prior to the departure of the flight, or if Alaska or another Carrier cancels the reservation of any Passenger, Alaska may cancel all reservations (whether or not confirmed) and seat assignments held by such Passenger for continuing or return space.
ambiguity_note: Alaska 'may' cancel; outcome is discretionary.

provenance.section: Rule 7. Cancellation of Reservations and Prohibited Practices

title: No Show forfeiture of funds
text: When a passenger does not notify Alaska prior to a flight's departure that he/she is unable to travel on their confirmed flight, the passenger is considered a "No Show" passenger and all segments associated with the reservation are automatically canceled and all funds or points used to purchase the ticket are forfeited, subject to the terms of Rule 17.
ambiguity_note: Forfeiture is subject to Rule 17, which is not included in this chunk; the cross-referenced terms determine the outcome.

provenance.section: Rule 7. Cancellation of Reservations and Prohibited Practices

title: Invalidation of tickets for prohibited practices
text: Alaska reserves the right to invalidate any Ticket(s) purchased or used in violation of this Contract of Carriage and Alaska's rules.
ambiguity_note: Discretionary right to invalidate; the scope of 'violation' is broad.

title: Sole discretion remedies on invalidated tickets
text: Where a Ticket is invalidated as the result of the Passenger's non-compliance with any term or condition of sale or any fare rule (including prohibitions on Back to Back Ticketing, Throwaway Ticketing, Hidden Cities Ticketing or Beyond Point Ticketing), Alaska has the right in its sole discretion to take all actions permitted by law, including, but not limited to, the following: (a) cancel any remaining portion of the Passenger's itinerary, (b) confiscate unused flight coupons, (c) refuse to board the Passenger or carry the Passenger's Baggage, unless the difference between the fare paid and the fare for transportation used is collected prior to boarding, (d) refuse to refund an otherwise refundable Ticket, (e) assess the Passenger for the actual remaining value of the Ticket, which shall be no less than the difference between the fare actually paid and the lowest fare applicable to the Passenger's actual itinerary, (f) delete points in the Passenger's frequent flyer account (Atmos Rewards), revoke the Passenger's Atmos Rewards status, if any, in Atmos Rewards, terminate the
ambiguity_note: Sole discretion remedies; the clause is truncated at the chunk boundary and the remaining remedies are not included.

title: Chargeback liability for ticket costs
text: In the event a Ticket becomes the subject of a credit card chargeback based upon impropriety, a non-sufficient funds check, a fraud or other form of compromised payment, the ticketed Passenger is liable for the Ticket costs plus an administrative fee.

title: Ticket not purchased from Alaska or authorized agent
text: A ticketed Passenger assumes all risk of loss for any Ticket not purchased from Alaska or an Alaska authorized travel agent.

title: Payment deadline for ticketing costs
text: Failure to pay ticketing costs and fees within sixty (60) days of notification may result in initiation of legal action or collection services.
ambiguity_note: States 'may result in' so outcome is discretionary.

title: Check-in time limits and cancellation right
text: Alaska reserves the right to cancel reservations (whether or not confirmed) and seat assignments, deny boarding and/or refuse the acceptance of Checked Baggage of any Passenger who fails to present himself/herself within the time limits preceding posted departure time of applicable flights as indicated in Section I of this Rule.
ambiguity_note: Reserves a right to cancel; outcome left to discretion.

title: Online ticket completion deadline
text: Tickets purchased on www.alaskaair.com, Alaska's mobile website or Alaska's mobile app must be completed at least sixty (60) minutes prior to posted departure, otherwise Alaska may cancel reservations and seat assignments of Tickets not yet purchased
ambiguity_note: Says Alaska 'may' cancel, so cancellation is discretionary.

title: Gate arrival deadline
text: Reservations and seat assignments may be canceled if Passenger fails to meet the check-in times noted in Rule 15.A.c, or fails to arrive for boarding at the gate at least 30 minutes prior to scheduled departure time.
ambiguity_note: 'May be canceled' leaves cancellation to discretion.

title: Late arrival may forfeit reservation
text: Reservations and seat assignments may be canceled and departures will not be delayed for Passengers who are improperly documented, or have not completed all security processing, have not met Alaska's check-in requirements, or are otherwise not ready to travel by the posted departure time.
ambiguity_note: 'May be canceled' is discretionary.

title: No liability for check-in cancellations
text: Alaska will not be liable for any consequential, compensatory, or other damages when it cancels the reservation (whether or not confirmed) of any Passenger in accordance with this Rule

title: Refund for check-in cancellation
text: If a reservation is cancelled pursuant to other paragraphs of this Rule, Alaska will refund in accordance with Rule 17 (Refunds-Voluntary).

title: Failure to operate schedule applies to paragraph A cancellations
text: if a reservation is cancelled pursuant to Paragraph A of this Rule, Rule 8 (Failure to Operate on Schedule) will apply.

title: Early departure discretion
text: Alaska reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to depart early when all Passengers who have met the requirements set forth in this Section I are onboard the aircraft.
ambiguity_note: Sole discretion to depart early.

title: Applicability of Rule 8 delay rights
text: The provisions of this Rule 8, other than for Section (F) below, apply to you only if you have a Ticket and a confirmed reserved space on one of our flights and there is a flight delay, flight change, flight diversion, or flight cancellation.

title: Standby passengers governed separately
text: If you are a standby guest, your rights are governed by Section (G) of this Rule 8.

title: Schedule changes not guaranteed
text: We may (i) substitute alternate carriers or aircraft, (ii) delay or cancel flights, and (iii) alter or omit stopping places or connections shown on the Ticket at any time.
ambiguity_note: 'May' grants discretion to change or cancel flights.

title: No liability for schedule changes
text: we are not liable for failing to operate any flight according to schedule, or for any change in flight schedule, with or without notice to you.

title: No liability for cancellations or significant delays
text: Without prejudice to any rights afforded under Applicable Laws, we are not liable for any Flight Cancellation or Significantly Delayed or Changed Flight.

title: Refund for cancelled or significantly delayed flight
text: When your ticket is affected by any flight cancellation or Significantly Delayed or Changed Flight, you have a nonrefundable ticket and we are the merchant of record, we will advise you of your right to a refund for any affected segments and refund your ticket in accordance with Rule 17, using the original form of payment, if: i. you decide not to fly on the Significantly Delayed or Changed Flight; ii. do not accept rebooking on an alternative flight we may offer you or we cannot offer you an alternative itinerary, and iii. do not accept a voucher, if offered to you.

title: Refund of fare difference for lower class
text: If we are unable to transport you in the same class of service you originally booked and you decide to travel in a lower class of service, we will provide a refund of the difference in fare.

title: EEA/UK compensation claim submission
text: A claim must be submitted directly to Alaska, either through Alaska's website or by writing to Alaska customer relations. The Passenger must allow Alaska 28 days (or such time as permitted by Applicable Law, whichever is the shorter) to respond, before engaging a third party to bring a claim on the Passenger's behalf.

title: Third-party claims not handled before 28-day process
text: Alaska will not deal with any claim submitted by a third party company on behalf of Passengers if the process at Rule 8 C.a. has not been followed.

title: Force majeure cancellation and refund
text: In the event of a Force Majeure Event, we may cancel, terminate, divert, postpone, or delay any flight, right of carriage, or reservations (whether or not confirmed) without any prior notice to you and determine if any departure or landing should be made, without any liability to Alaska, subject to Applicable Laws. We may offer to re-accommodate you on another available Alaska flight or on another carrier or combination of carriers, or may refund you or provide you a travel certificate for any unused portions of your ticket.
ambiguity_note: Refund or travel certificate is at Alaska's discretion ('may refund ... or provide a travel certificate').

title: Hotel accommodations for lengthy delay
text: If you experience an overnight stay at an airport located 100 or more miles away from your home because your flight is canceled or delayed due to circumstances within our control, complimentary hotel accommodations will be provided if there are available hotels in the area where the delay or cancellation occurs.
ambiguity_note: Depends on availability of hotels in the area; 'available hotels' is not defined.

title: Meals during lengthy delay
text: We will offer a reasonable meal to each ticket guest at the airport if the delay will extend beyond three (3) hours.
ambiguity_note: Meal offered is described as 'reasonable' and specific options depend on vendor availability.

title: Ground transportation reimbursement
text: When lodging is provided to you in accordance with Section (E)(1) above of this Rule 8 and ground transportation is not furnished by the hotel, then, if available, we will provide ground transportation to the place of lodging or reimburse you for reasonable transportation expenses when accompanied by a receipt.
ambiguity_note: Conditional on availability and receipt; 'reasonable' is undefined.

title: Travel credit in lieu of amenities
text: We may provide you a with a travel credit in lieu of any of the above. Your acceptance of a travel credit indicates your waiver of any of the above amenities.
ambiguity_note: Alaska may choose to offer a credit instead of amenities at its discretion.

title: Travel credit terms
text: Travel credit (i) will be valid for travel only on Alaska operated flights within one year of the date of issue, (ii) will apply only to online transportation via Alaska, (iii) may not be endorsed to or accepted by any other carrier, and (iv) is not refundable, nor saleable, transferable, or assignable by you.

title: Schedule change liability
text: Except to the extent provided in Section (G)(2) below of this Rule 8, we are not liable for failing to operate any flight according to schedule, or for any change in flight schedule, with or without notice to you.

title: Options when schedule is changed or missed
text: Whenever we fail to operate any flight according to schedule or change the schedule of any flight, we will, at your request, either: i. transport you on another of our flights on which space is available; or ii. refund you an amount determined in accordance with Rule 17: Refunds upon surrender of the unused portion of your Ticket will be made using the original form of payment.
ambiguity_note: Refund amount is determined by reference to Rule 17, not stated here.

title: Oversold flight from outside U.S. or Canada
text: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein, where there is an oversold Alaska flight that originates outside the U.S.A. or Canada, no compensation will be provided except where required by Applicable Laws regulating oversold flights.
ambiguity_note: Compensation depends on Applicable Laws, which are not specified here.

title: Voluntary denied boarding compensation
text: If a flight is oversold (more Passengers hold confirmed reservations than there are seats available), no Passenger may be denied boarding against his or her will until Alaska's personnel first ask for volunteers who are willing to relinquish their confirmed reserved space voluntarily in exchange for compensation in an amount determined by Alaska (including, but not limited to, a check or an electronic travel certificate).
ambiguity_note: Compensation amount is determined solely by Alaska.

title: Travel certificate for volunteers
text: The travel certificate will be valid only for Carriage on Alaska or one of our regional partners for one year from the date of issue and will have no refund value.

title: Involuntary denied boarding notice requirement
text: If a Passenger is asked to volunteer, Alaska will not later deny boarding to that Passenger involuntarily unless the Passenger was informed at the time he/she was asked to volunteer that there was a possibility of being denied boarding involuntarily and of the amount of compensation to which he/she would have been entitled in that event.

title: Boarding priority order
text: Passengers will be boarded in the following order until all available seats are occupied: (1) All Passengers holding confirmed seat assignments will be boarded; and (2) Passengers who are not holding confirmed seat assignments will be boarded in order of the time they check in

title: Exceptions to boarding priority
text: Possible exceptions may be made in the case of Unaccompanied Minors, Qualified Individuals with a Disability, or any other Passenger, who in Alaska's opinion, may suffer severe hardship. Business commitments will not, of themselves, constitute a severe hardship.
ambiguity_note: Exceptions are at Alaska's opinion; 'severe hardship' is discretionary.

title: Transportation for passengers denied boarding
text: Alaska will transport Passengers denied boarding, whether voluntarily or involuntarily, without Stopover on its next flight on which space is available at no additional cost to the Passenger regardless of class of service, and if unable to provide onward transportation acceptable to the Passenger, at Alaska's sole discretion and the request of the Passenger, will transport the Passenger by other Carrier or combination of
ambiguity_note: Onward transport by other carrier is at Alaska's sole discretion; text is truncated at chunk boundary.

title: Re-routing without Stopover at no extra cost if earlier arrival
text: Such flight(s) will be used without Stopover at no additional cost to the Passenger only if it (they) will provide an earlier arrival at the Passenger's destination, next Stopover point, or transfer point.

title: Compensation for involuntary denied boarding due to oversale
text: In addition to providing transportation as described in Paragraph d above, Passengers involuntarily denied boarding will be compensated for Alaska's failure to provide confirmed space in accordance with the provisions below.

title: Eligibility conditions for denied boarding compensation
text: In order to receive denied boarding compensation, the Passenger holding a Ticket for confirmed reserved space must have presented himself/herself for Carriage in accordance with this Contract of Carriage, and must have complied fully with Alaska's requirements as to ticketing, check-in, and boarding requirements within the time limits and at the location set out in Rule 15.C.

title: Denied boarding eligibility: flight must depart without passenger
text: In addition, the flight for which the Passenger holds confirmed reserved space must be unable to accommodate the Passenger and departs without him/her

title: Exclusion: cancelled flight or operational/safety reasons
text: the Passenger will not be eligible for compensation if: (i) the flight on which he/she holds confirmed reserved space is cancelled or is unable to accommodate him/her because of government requisition of space, operational or safety reasons, or substitution of aircraft type of lesser capacity and Alaska took all reasonable measures to avoid the substitution or it was impossible to take such measures
ambiguity_note: 'All reasonable measures' is a discretionary standard not quantified in the text.

title: Exclusion: weight/balance restriction on small aircraft
text: (ii) on a flight operated with an aircraft having 60 or fewer seats, the Passenger is denied boarding due to a safety-related weight/balance restriction that limits payload

title: Exclusion: accommodation in another section at no extra charge
text: (iii) the Passenger is offered accommodations in a section of the aircraft other than specified in their Ticket, at no extra charge (a Passenger seated in a section for which a lower fare is charged must be given an appropriate refund)
ambiguity_note: 'Appropriate refund' is not quantified.

title: Exclusion: alternate flight within one hour
text: (iv) Alaska is able to place the Passenger on another flight or flights that are planned to reach the Passenger's next Stopover or final destination within one hour of the planned arrival time of their original flight

title: Exclusion: employees and non-confirmed passengers
text: (v) the Passenger is an employee of Alaska or of another Carrier or other Passenger traveling without a confirmed reserved space

title: Check-in time limit failure forfeits denied boarding compensation
text: Failure to comply with Alaska check-in time limits will result in the cancellation of the Passenger's reservation and will render him/her ineligible for denied boarding compensation.

title: Domestic denied boarding: no compensation if alternate arrives within one hour
text: No compensation if Alaska offers alternate transportation that, at the time the arrangement is made, is planned to arrive at the Passenger's destination or first Stopover not later than one (1) hour after the planned arrival time of the Passenger's original flight

title: Domestic denied boarding: 200% fare up to $1,075 for 1-2 hour arrival delay
text: At least 200% of the fare to the Passenger's destination or first Stopover, or $1,075, whichever is lower, if Alaska offers alternate transportation that, at the time the arrangement is made, is planned to arrive at the Passenger's destination or first Stopover more than one (1) hour but less than two (2) hours after the planned arrival time of the Passenger's original flight

provenance.section: I. Amount of Denied Boarding Compensation

title: Domestic denied boarding: 400% fare up to $2,150 for over 2 hour delay
text: At least 400% of the fare to the Passenger's destination or first Stopover, or $2,150, whichever is lower, if Alaska does not offer alternate transportation that, at the time the arrangement is made, is planned to arrive at the airport of the Passenger's destination or first Stopover more than two (2) hours after the planned arrival time of the Passenger's original flight.

provenance.section: I. Amount of Denied Boarding Compensation

title: International denied boarding from US: 200% fare up to $1075 for 1-4 hour delay
text: At least 200% of the fare to the Passenger's destination or first Stopover, or $1075, whichever is lower, if Alaska offers alternate transportation that, at the time the arrangement is made, is planned to arrive at the Passenger's destination or first Stopover more than one (1) hour but less than four (4) hours after the planned arrival time of the Passenger's original flight

title: Canada-originating denied boarding: maximum $400 CAD for 1-4 hour delay
text: A maximum payment of $400 CAD if Alaska offers alternate transportation that, at the time the arrangement is made, is planned to arrive at the Passenger's destination or first Stopover more than one (1) hour but less than four (4) hours after the planned arrival time of the Passenger's original flight

title: Canada-originating denied boarding: maximum $800 CAD for over 4 hour delay
text: A maximum payment of $800 CAD if Alaska offers alternate transportation that, at the time the arrangement is made, is planned to arrive at the Passenger's destination or first Stopover more than four (4) hours after the planned arrival time of the Passenger's original flight.

title: Denied boarding from outside US/Canada: local law governs
text: Where there is an Oversold Flight that originates outside the U.S.A. or Canada, no compensation will be provided except where required by local or international laws regulating Oversold Flights.
ambiguity_note: Depends on local or international laws not specified in the document.

title: UK/EEA denied boarding compensation per Applicable Law
text: Passengers travelling from an airport located in the UK or the EEA, who are denied boarding against their will on a flight on which they have a valid ticket and confirmed reservation, will be entitled to compensation, refreshments and other care and assistance as required by Applicable Law.
ambiguity_note: Amount is determined by Applicable Law, not stated in the document.

title: Korea departures: KFTC guideline standards
text: Passengers denied boarding, facing flight cancellations, or experiencing delays of at least two hours are entitled to treatment and compensation according to the standards set by the Korea Fair Trade Commission's Consumer Dispute Resolution Guidelines. However, Alaska Airlines may provide compensation exceeding these standards under special circumstances.
ambiguity_note: 'Special circumstances' is undefined and discretionary.

text: if Alaska arranges alternate transportation for the Passenger's convenience that departs before the payment can be made, the payment shall be sent by mail or other means to the Passenger within 24 hours after the time the denied boarding occurs.

title: Free or discounted transportation in place of denied boarding cash
text: Alaska may offer free or discounted air transportation in place of the cash payment due under this Rule, if the value of the air transportation offered is equal to or greater than the monetary compensation otherwise due and Alaska informs the Passenger of the amount and that the Passenger may decline the transportation benefit and receive monetary compensation.

text: In that event, Alaska must disclose all material restrictions on the use of the free or discounted transportation before the Passenger decides whether to accept the transportation in lieu of a cash or check payment.

text: For each Passenger who qualifies for involuntary denied boarding compensation on a flight departing from the UK or the EEA, such compensation shall be paid in cash, bank check or electronic reimbursement to original payment method.

title: Acceptance of denied boarding compensation is full settlement
text: Acceptance of the compensation by the Passenger pursuant to the above provisions in this Rule constitutes full compensation for all actual or anticipatory damages incurred or to be incurred by the Passenger as a result of Alaska's failure to provide the Passenger with confirmed reserved space and relieves Alaska from any further liability to the Passenger caused by Alaska's failure to honor the confirmed reservation.

title: Denied boarding liability cap if compensation not accepted
text: If Alaska's offer of compensation pursuant to the above provisions is not accepted, Alaska's liability is limited to actual damages proved not to exceed $2150 USD per ticketed Passenger as a result of Alaska's failure to provide the Passenger with confirmed reserved space.
