title: Passenger must document actual damages
text: Passenger will be responsible for providing documentation of all actual damages claimed.

provenance.section: Consumer Dispute Resolution Guidelines. However, Alaska Airlines

title: No punitive, consequential or special damages for denied boarding
text: Alaska shall not be liable for any punitive, consequential or special damages arising out of or in connection with Alaska's failure to provide the Passenger with confirmed reserved space.

provenance.section: Consumer Dispute Resolution Guidelines. However, Alaska Airlines

title: Passenger may decline payment and sue
text: However, the Passenger may decline the payment and seek to recover damages in a court of law or in some other manner.

provenance.section: Consumer Dispute Resolution Guidelines. However, Alaska Airlines

title: Baggage monitoring and inspection; refusal to transport
text: All Baggage is subject to monitoring and inspection by Alaska and/or authorized government agencies with or without the Passenger's consent or knowledge; however, Alaska shall not be obligated to perform monitoring and inspection. Alaska may refuse to transport on any flight or may remove at any point Baggage that the Passenger refuses to submit for inspection.

title: Baggage carried on different flight when space unavailable
text: Alaska may refuse to transport Baggage on any flight other than the one carrying the Passenger. Checked Baggage will generally be carried on the same aircraft as the Passenger unless such carriage is deemed impractical by Alaska, in which event Alaska will make arrangements to transport the Baggage on the next flight on which space is available.
ambiguity_note: 'generally' and 'deemed impractical by Alaska' leave the outcome to Alaska's discretion.

title: Baggage refused for unsuitable size, weight, or packaging
text: Alaska may also refuse to accept property (except for Assistive Devices) for transportation whose size, weight, contents, type of packaging or character renders it unsuitable for transportation on the particular aircraft which is to transport it; which cannot be accommodated without harming or annoying Passengers; or which is not suitably or adequately packaged to withstand ordinary handling.
ambiguity_note: Suitability and adequate packaging are determined by Alaska without objective thresholds.

title: Baggage identification responsibility
text: Each piece of Checked Baggage tendered to Alaska must have a current identification tag or label with the Passenger's name, address, and telephone number. It is the Passenger's responsibility to attach proper identification to Baggage, and Alaska is not liable for a Passenger's failure to do so.

title: Passenger responsible for claiming checked baggage
text: It is also the Passenger's responsibility to claim the Checked Baggage at the Baggage claim area, and Alaska assumes no obligation to verify the identity of the owner of the Baggage at the destination airport.

title: Hazardous or injurious baggage not accepted
text: Alaska will not accept Baggage that, because of its nature, contents, or characteristics (e.g., sharp objects, paint, corrosives, or other prohibited hazardous materials), might cause injury to Passengers or Alaska, damage to aircraft or other equipment, or damage to other Baggage.

title: Baggage that cannot safely be carried not accepted
text: Alaska will not accept Baggage that it determines cannot safely be carried in the Baggage compartment of the aircraft for any reason.
ambiguity_note: 'determines' and 'for any reason' give Alaska unrestricted discretion.

title: Same-day baggage tendered too early not accepted
text: Alaska will not accept, store or hold Baggage from a Passenger on the day of travel at Alaska's airport Ticket counter or curbside check-in locations (where available) if tendered to Alaska earlier than four (4) hours in advance of flight departure time.

title: Carry-on baggage may be checked by Alaska for any reason
text: Alaska reserves the right to check a Passenger's Carry-on Baggage for any reason, including if the Carry-on Baggage cannot be safely stowed.
ambiguity_note: Alaska may act 'for any reason' without defined criteria.

title: Checked baggage requires valid ticket and applicable fee
text: Alaska will check Baggage, acceptable under Alaska's rules, which is tendered by a Passenger holding a valid Ticket for transportation on Alaska, or over the lines of Alaska and one or more other Carriers, subject to payment of the applicable fee (see below) and the following conditions

title: Checked baggage minimum check-in times
text: Alaska may refuse to accept any article of Checked Baggage that has not been presented, checked in, and processed in accordance with our policies on minimum required check-in and boarding cut-off times
ambiguity_note: Minimum times are defined by a website policy referenced rather than stated in the document.

title: Late-checked baggage not guaranteed on flight
text: Baggage checked in less than the minimum time required may be accepted and Alaska will make reasonable efforts, but cannot guarantee, to transport such Baggage on the Passenger's flight(s). Alaska will not assume responsibility for delivery charges if such Baggage arrives at the Passenger's destination on a subsequent flight.
ambiguity_note: 'reasonable efforts' is undefined; no guarantee of carriage.

title: Codeshare check-in requirements
text: Additional passenger and baggage check-in requirements may apply on flights operated by Alaska's Codeshare Partners. These requirements may be found in the Codeshare Partners' contracts of carriage, which are available on those Carriers' websites.

title: Checked baggage acceptance up to four hours before departure
text: Alaska will accept Checked Baggage up to four (4) hours prior to scheduled departure time. Exception: Ticket counters which open less than four (4) hours prior to departure will accept bags when the Ticket counter opens.

title: Baggage not checked to points off routing or beyond destination
text: Baggage will not be checked: To a point that is not on the Passenger's routing. Beyond the Passenger's next point of Stopover or, if there is no Stopover, beyond the final destination designated on the Ticket. Beyond a point at which the Passenger wants to reclaim the Baggage or any portion thereof. Beyond the point to which all applicable charges have been paid. Beyond a point at which the Passenger is to transfer to a connecting flight, if that flight is scheduled to depart from an airport different from the one at which the Passenger is scheduled to arrive.

title: Live animals not checked beyond transfer point
text: Live Animals will not be checked beyond a point of transfer to another Carrier, except on flights operated by one of our regional partners.

title: Carry-on baggage storage and size determined by Alaska
text: When Baggage is carried on board the aircraft, it must be stored under a seat or in an overhead compartment. The suitability of Baggage as to weight, size, contents, and character will be solely determined by Alaska.
ambiguity_note: Suitability is solely at Alaska's determination with no stated criteria.

title: Free carry-on allowance
text: Each ticketed Passenger is allowed one Carry-On Bag and one small personal item.

title: Carry-on bag dimension limit
text: The Carry-On Bag dimensions must not exceed 9" in height by 14" in width by 22" in length.

title: Carry-on must be manageable by one passenger
text: Carry-On Baggage and small personal items must be capable of being carried onboard the aircraft by one Passenger without additional assistance (except for a Qualified Individual with a Disability requiring assistance due to their disability) and must be capable of being stowed under a seat or in an overhead compartment.

title: Items exceeding free allowance are charged
text: Items exceeding the free allowance (see exceptions below) will be charged as indicated in Section 15.F and tagged for delivery to Baggage claim at the Passenger's destination.

title: Carry-on piece limit exceptions
text: All items brought onboard count toward the Carry-On Baggage and small personal item piece limit except the following: Coats, hats, or umbrellas; Reasonable amount of reading material; Infant/Child safety seats, baby carrier backpack, strollers (based on space availability; space guaranteed only with the purchase of a Ticket for the Infant); Mobility/Medical Assistive Devices; Service Animals; Food for immediate consumption; and A pillow for personal use.
ambiguity_note: Reasonable amount of reading material is undefined; stroller and car seat space is based on availability.

title: Oversize carry-on exceptions
text: The following items count as the "one" free Carry-On Bag and may exceed the Carry-On Baggage dimensions as long as they can be safely accommodated in a proper stowage compartment in the cabin of the aircraft: Human organs; Art/Advertising portfolios; Paintings; Delicate scientific equipment; Fishing poles; or Duty Free Items.
ambiguity_note: Depends on whether a proper stowage compartment is available in the cabin.

title: Carry-on restriction reserved
text: Alaska reserves the right to further restrict the number of Carry-On Bags and small personal items carried onboard its flights.
ambiguity_note: Discretionary restriction with no stated criteria.

title: Checked baggage charges apply
text: Baggage exceeding the free Carry-On Baggage allowance shall be checked and will be accepted for transportation (subject to aircraft load conditions) only upon payment of the following charges.
ambiguity_note: Charge amounts are defined only by external web link; subject to aircraft load conditions.

title: Checked bag charges reapplied after stopover
text: Checked Baggage charges must be paid again by Passengers who continue their journey and check bags after a Stopover of twelve (12) hours or more.

title: Space-available baggage
text: Due to limited aircraft size, limited cargo hold capacity and restricted gross take-off weights, excess, oversized and/or overweight Baggage presented or transferred at departure time without a prearranged reservation for space may travel on a space-available basis.
ambiguity_note: Space-available outcome depends on aircraft capacity at departure.

title: Car seats, strollers and assistive devices checked free
text: Car seats, baby carrier backpacks, strollers, and Assistive Devices may be checked without incurring a Baggage service charge.

title: Domestic overweight charge threshold
text: Domestic Overweight Charge - Checked Baggage (including Baggage accepted free of charge) may not exceed 50 lbs./32 kg. without incurring an overweight charge.

title: Overweight charge per piece
text: Each piece over 50 lbs./23kg. , the charge shall be as defined at https://www.alaskaair.com/content/travel-info/baggage/checked-bags
ambiguity_note: Charge amount is defined only by external link; the document states 50 lbs./32 kg. and 23kg inconsistently.

title: Military overweight exception
text: Active duty U.S. military Passengers and military recruit Passengers and their dependents eligible for the U.S. military Baggage charge waiver may check bags which weigh 70 lbs./32 kg. or less without incurring an overweight fee. Bags weighing 71-100 lbs./ 32-45 kg. shall follow the standard overweight charge noted above if allowed on route.
ambiguity_note: Weight units are inconsistent (70 lbs./32 kg.) and the 'if allowed on route' condition is undefined.

title: Domestic oversize charge threshold
text: Domestic Oversized Charge - Checked Baggage may not exceed 62 inches without incurring an oversize charge.

title: Maximum bag weight
text: Baggage that weighs more than 100 lbs./45 kg. per piece will not be accepted.

title: Military oversize exception
text: Active duty U.S. military Passengers and military recruit Passengers and their dependents eligible for the U.S. military Baggage charge waiver may check bags up to 115 linear inches without incurring an oversize charge.

title: Excess baggage not accepted on certain flights
text: Excess, oversize and/or overweight Baggage may not be accepted on certain flights as solely determined by Alaska.
ambiguity_note: Flight acceptance determined solely by Alaska with no stated criteria.

title: Discretionary baggage allowance exceptions
text: Alaska may, at its sole discretion, change, consider and make exceptions to its Baggage Allowance policy (e.g., to the number, size, weight, type, and/or applicable service charges) for certain Atmos Rewards members, active duty U.S. military Passengers, and/or other Passengers depending on the fare class purchased or cities flown.
ambiguity_note: Sole discretion with no defined criteria for exceptions.

title: Excess baggage connecting airline charges
text: Baggage connecting to other airlines will also be subject to the connecting airline's excess charges, in addition to the carrier's excess charges.

title: Baggage refused when oversize or overweight
text: NOTE: Baggage will not be accepted for carriage when the maximum outside or linear dimensions are more than 206 centimeters or 80 inches, or when the weight exceeds 100 lbs./45 kg.

title: Exception for 70 lb limit on Australia/NZ/Cook Islands/Papeete routes
text: Exception: Baggage for travel between the United States and Australia, New Zealand, Cook Islands or French Polynesia (Papeete, PPT) that weighs more than 70lbs./32 kg. per piece will not be accepted.

title: International overweight pieces 50 to 70 lb charges
text: Items that are in excess of the baggage weight allowances where the allowance is 50 lbs./23 kg. and up to 70 lb./32 kg. will be charged the following additional per piece overweight charges as defined at https://www.alaskaair.com/content/travel-info/baggage/checked-bags:
ambiguity_note: Charge amounts are referenced at an external URL and not stated in the document.

title: International overweight pieces 70 to 100 lb charges
text: Items that are in excess of 70 lbs./32 kg. and up to 100 lbs./45kg., will always be subject to the following per piece charges found at https://www.alaskaair.com/content/travel-info/baggage/checked-bags, except for travel between the United States and Australia/New Zealand/Cook Islands/French Polynesia (Papeete) for which items in excess of 70 lbs./32 kg. will not be accepted:
ambiguity_note: Charge amounts are referenced at an external URL and not stated in the document.

title: Live animal acceptance at Alaska's discretion
text: Alaska will accept domesticated cats, dogs, ferrets, guinea pigs, hamsters, household birds, non-poisonous reptiles, potbellied pigs, rabbits, and tropical fish for transportation at Alaska's discretion, and subject to the conditions below:
ambiguity_note: Acceptance is at Alaska's discretion with no objective criteria stated.

title: Live animal fees nonrefundable
text: The animal fees found on https://www.alaskaair.com/content/travel-info/optional-services-fees must be collected prior to flight, are nonrefundable, and may not be applied toward future travel if unused.
ambiguity_note: Fee amounts are referenced at an external URL and not stated in the document.

title: Animal refusal and removal at Alaska's discretion
text: Alaska retains the right, at its sole discretion, to refuse to transport any animal that exhibits aggressive behavior or any characteristics that appear to Alaska to be incompatible with air travel at the airport, in the boarding gate area, or onboard the aircraft.
ambiguity_note: Refusal is at Alaska's sole discretion with no objective standard.

title: Live animal liability disclaimer
text: Alaska assumes no liability for the health or wellbeing of carry-on animals.

title: Health certificate and entry requirement costs
text: Alaska Airlines will not be responsible for any costs incurred should the Passenger not meet their animal's health and vaccination requirements for their destination.

title: Animal carrier size limit in cabin
text: Only soft-sided carriers are accepted in the Passenger compartment, with maximum dimension of 17 in. by 11 in. by 9.5 in.

title: Unaccompanied minors may not travel with animal in cabin
text: Unaccompanied Minors may not travel with an animal in the Passenger compartment.

title: Muzzled, pregnant, injured or ill animals refused
text: Muzzled, pregnant, injured or ill animals will not be accepted for Carriage.

title: Passenger responsible for animal legal compliance
text: The Passenger must make all arrangements and assume full responsibility for complying with all Applicable Laws, customs, and/or other governmental regulations, requirements, or restrictions of the country, state, or territory to which the animal is being transported, including furnishing a valid health and rabies vaccination certificate when required. Alaska will not be liable for loss or expense due to the Passenger's failure to comply with this provision.

title: Seat change for animal passengers
text: Alaska Airlines reserves the right to change the seat assignment of the Passenger traveling with animals for safety or administrative reasons.
ambiguity_note: Discretionary seat change; not a post-purchase refund or compensation outcome.

title: Brachycephalic animals not accepted as checked baggage
text: The following breeds of brachycephalic dogs and cats (or any mix thereof), are not accepted for transport as Checked Baggage except for direct flights between the State of Hawaii and the U.S. Mainland or interisland flights within the State of Hawaii (no U.S. Mainland connecting flights allowed):

title: Release from liability for snub-nosed animals
text: By checking in any snub-nosed or short-nosed dog(s) or cat(s) for transportation in the cargo compartment for any reason, the Passenger: (1) acknowledges and accepts the warning about the increased health risks to snub-nosed or short-nosed animal(s); (2) releases Alaska from all liability, claims, or damages resulting from the transportation of any snub-nosed or short-nosed animal(s); and (3) agrees not to file any claim with Alaska relating to the transportation of any snub-nosed or short-nosed animal(s).

title: Unacceptable in-cabin animals
text: Alaska will not accept dogs of the Pit Bull breed (unless Service Animal), snakes, other reptiles, ferrets, rodents and spiders as in-cabin Carry-On Baggage.

title: Other in-cabin animals at Alaska's discretion
text: Carriage of any other animals as in-cabin Carry-On Baggage will be at Alaska’s discretion.
ambiguity_note: Acceptance left to Alaska's discretion without stated criteria.

title: No liability for animal illness or injury
text: Alaska will not be liable for illness or injury to an animal or death of an animal due to illness or injury when the animal has been handled by Alaska with ordinary standards of safety and care or when Alaska has acted in the interests of the entire flight such as in an emergency or a Force Majeure Event.

title: Live animal fees apply to all passengers
text: The charges outlined are applicable for all Passengers, including those whose Checked Baggage charges are waived.

title: Codeshare live animal rules apply
text: When flights are operated by Codeshare Partners, the Codeshare Partner's rules and fees for live animal transportation apply.

title: Unclaimed animal placed in kennel at passenger expense
text: If the animal is not called for within 6 hours after flight arrival, the animal will be placed in a local kennel at the Passenger's expense.

title: Animal deemed abandoned after ten days
text: An animal that is unclaimed by its owner or its owner’s agent for a period of more than ten (10) days after the scheduled Carriage has occurred or was to occur, shall be deemed abandoned and may be turned over to a local animal shelter or pound or otherwise handled as Alaska may deem proper without any liability to Alaska.
ambiguity_note: 'Otherwise handled as Alaska may deem proper' leaves handling to discretion.

title: Reunion costs borne by owner
text: Any costs associated with reuniting an animal deemed abandoned with its owner or owner’s agent shall be borne solely by the owner or owner’s agent.

title: Passenger responsible for Hawaii animal requirements
text: The Passenger is solely responsible for understanding and complying with State of Hawaii requirements before traveling.

title: Animals accepted to and from Hawaii
text: Dogs and cats are the only animals accepted to/from Hawaii. Birds may be accepted for interisland travel within the State of Hawaii only.

title: Interline transfers not permitted to Hawaii
text: Interline transfers are not permitted to Hawaii.

title: Neighbor Island permit required for cats and dogs
text: If the document requirement is not met, the animal will not be allowed to travel.

title: Hawaii quarantine of dogs and cats
text: Dogs and cats may be quarantined for up to 120 days upon arrival in the State of Hawaii unless they meet all the State’s 5-Day-Or-Less program requirements, which include certain pet vaccinations, a blood test, and waiting periods.

title: Bassinets not accepted
text: Bassinets are not accepted. Infant carrying seats approved by the U.S. DOT or comparable foreign agency are accepted free of charge.

title: Fragile or perishable items packaging condition
text: Fragile and/or perishable items (for examples, see Paragraph d below) will be accepted as Checked Baggage in accordance with this Rule only if they are appropriately packaged in an original factory-sealed carton, cardboard mailing tube, or container or case designed for shipping such items or packed with protective internal material.
ambiguity_note: 'Fragile, perishable or inappropriately packaged articles may be accepted from time-to-time' leaves acceptance discretionary.

title: No liability for inherent defect or wear of fragile baggage
text: Alaska is not responsible or liable for loss or damage of contents or delay in delivery resulting in damage or loss of the checked baggage where such loss or damage results solely from the inherent defect, quality or vice of the baggage or is due to fair wear and tear resulting from ordinary handling of baggage.

title: No liability for damage caused by fragile items in carry-on
text: Alaska is not liable for damage to a Passenger’s Carry-On Baggage or other in-cabin property that contains fragile or perishable items when such damage is caused by the fragile or perishable items.

title: Passenger responsible for damage caused by their property
text: Passengers are responsible for all damage caused by their property, whether such damage is to their own property or to someone else’s property.

title: Classes of items deemed fragile or unsuitable as checked baggage
text: The classes of items listed below are deemed to be fragile or perishable or otherwise unsuitable as Checked Baggage and are subject to the conditions of acceptance set forth in paragraph b above.

title: Dry ice limit
text: A maximum of 5.5lbs/2.5 kg. of dry ice per Passenger will be accepted for carriage as Checked Baggage or Carry-On Baggage provided the Baggage is properly designed to permit the release of carbon dioxide, and the container is labeled, “DRY ICE” or “CARBON DIOXIDE SOLID.”

title: Alcohol over 70 percent not accepted
text: Alcoholic beverages more than 70 percent alcohol by volume will not be accepted;

title: Liquor breakage liability
text: All alcoholic beverages must be packed to prevent leakage and damage to other Baggage. Alaska shall not be liable for breakage or spillage of alcoholic beverages.

title: Musical instrument size and weight limits
text: Checked instruments cannot exceed 165lbs./75kg. and 150 linear inches (or the applicable weight/size restriction for the aircraft) and will be included in determining the Baggage allowance, and when in excess (over 2 checked items), overweight or oversize, will be subject to the excess, oversize, and overweight Baggage charge.

title: Musical instrument damage liability
text: Except for certain International Carriage subject to the terms of the Montreal Convention or Warsaw Convention, whichever may apply, Alaska is not liable for damage to musical instruments or musical instrument cases.
ambiguity_note: Exclusion is subject to international convention exceptions whose application is not specified in this text.

title: Fragile items release advisory
text: Where Passengers elect to transport fragile items without appropriate packaging, Alaska will not be liable for damage to such items in Checked Baggage, where damage results solely from the unsuitability of such items as Checked Baggage and/or the inherent defect, quality or vice of the Checked Baggage, except for certain International Carriage of such fragile items subject to the terms of the Montreal Convention or Warsaw Convention, whichever may apply.
ambiguity_note: Liability exclusion applies only where damage results 'solely' from unsuitability or inherent defect; international convention exceptions apply.

title: Perishable spoilage from delay not liable
text: Nor will Alaska be liable for spoilage or substantial loss of value or potency which results from delay in delivery of Checked Baggage when such spoilage results solely from the unsuitability of such items as Checked Baggage and/or the inherent defect, quality or vice of the Checked Baggage, except for certain International Carriage of such items subject to the terms of the Montreal Convention or Warsaw Convention, whichever may apply.
ambiguity_note: Exclusion applies only where spoilage results solely from unsuitability or inherent defect; international convention exceptions apply.

title: Wet ice not accepted
text: Alaska will not accept wet ice or items containing wet ice as Checked Baggage or Carry-On Baggage.

title: Child/Infant car seats accepted in addition to baggage allowance
text: car seats approved for airline travel, will be accepted in addition to a Passenger’s Baggage allowance. When checked as Baggage, all oversize and overweight charges will apply. First and second bag charges do not apply.

title: Child/Infant seat in cabin conditions
text: A government-approved Child/Infant seat for use in the Passenger compartment is permitted only when an additional seat is reserved for the Infant, a Ticket is purchased, and the seat can be secured properly by a seat belt.

title: No liability for damage to checked Child/Infant seats
text: Except for certain International Carriage subject to the terms of the Montreal Convention or Warsaw Convention, whichever may apply, Alaska is not liable for damage to Child/Infant seats when carried as Checked Baggage.

title: One collapsible stroller accepted in addition to baggage allowance
text: Alaska accepts one collapsible stroller in addition to a Passenger’s Baggage allowance.

title: Non-collapsible stroller as checked baggage
text: One non-collapsible stroller may be carried as Checked Baggage in lieu of one piece of Baggage (62 inches Maximum Outside Linear Dimensions). This item will be included in determining the Baggage allowance, and when in excess, overweight or oversize, such item will be subject to the excess Baggage charge.

title: No liability for damage to checked strollers
text: Except for certain International Carriage subject to the terms of the Montreal Convention or Warsaw Convention, whichever may apply, Alaska is not liable for damage to strollers when carried as Checked Baggage.

title: No excess valuation for strollers
text: Excess valuation may not be purchased for strollers.

title: One wheelchair per passenger accepted free
text: One wheelchair per Passenger will be accepted as Baggage by Alaska at no extra charge in addition to the Passenger’s Baggage allowance.

title: Additional recreational wheelchairs charged
text: Excess and/or oversize/overweight Baggage charges pursuant to this Rule 15 may apply for checking in additional wheelchair(s) that are used for recreational purposes.
ambiguity_note: Says charges 'may apply'; outcome left to discretion and no amount stated.

title: Wet cell battery wheelchair notice and check-in requirements
text: For a wet cell battery-powered wheelchair, the Passenger must notify Alaska at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance, the Passenger must check in at least one (1) hour before the check-in time for the general public, and the battery must be disconnected and terminals protected against electrical shortages.

title: Lithium ion wheelchair batteries 300 WH and above refused
text: Wheelchairs containing lithium ion batteries with a watt hour rating of 300 WH and above will not be accepted under any circumstances.

title: Wheelchairs with non-spillable or small lithium batteries accepted
text: Wheelchairs containing non-spillable batteries or lithium ion batteries with a watt hour rating of 300 WH or less may be carried on as Baggage or may be checked.
ambiguity_note: Uses 'may be carried on or checked'; permissive wording, handling left unspecified.

title: Restricted hazardous articles not accepted as baggage
text: Articles listed in the DOT Hazardous Materials Regulations (49 C.F.R. Parts 171-180) and/or IATA dangerous goods regulations and revisions and reissues thereof, will not be accepted for Carriage as Baggage except for dry ice and small arms ammunition (as specified in Paragraph J(12) of this Rule).

title: Sporting items over 115 linear inches not accepted as checked
text: Items over 115 linear inches (length plus height plus width) shall not be accepted as checked baggage unless noted in this section.

title: Sporting items 100 lbs or greater not accepted as checked
text: Items that are 100 lbs./45 kg. or greater shall not be accepted as Checked Baggage.

title: Sporting equipment not liable for damage when checked
text: Except for certain International Carriage subject to the terms of the Montreal Convention or Warsaw Convention, whichever may apply, Alaska is not liable for damage to the items specified below when carried as Checked Baggage.

title: Antlers acceptance conditions
text: Antlers will only be accepted as Checked Baggage when they are properly packaged in an enclosed container acceptable to Alaska and meet normal size and weight restrictions.

title: Archery equipment as one checked piece
text: One piece of archery equipment consisting of a proper soft or hard archery case containing bows and arrows may be checked in lieu of one piece of Checked Baggage as long as the bow and arrows are encased in a container acceptable to Alaska for withstanding normal Baggage handling without sustaining damage to the equipment.
ambiguity_note: 'Acceptable to Alaska' container standard is at Alaska's discretion.

title: Archery pieces 51 lbs or heavier exempt from oversize charge
text: Checked archery pieces weighing 51 lbs./23 kg. or greater, or exceeding 62 linear inches may be checked without being assessed an oversize/overweight charge.

title: Bicycle packing requirements
text: Alaska will only accept bicycles properly packed in a hard-sided bicycle box or container, with handlebars turned sideways, protruding pedals and accessories removed, and all sharp protrusions padded so as not to be damaged by or cause damage to other Baggage.

title: Bicycles 51-70 lbs or over 62 inches exempt from oversize charge
text: Checked bicycles weighing 51–70 lbs./23-32 kg. or exceeding 62 linear inches, may be checked without being assessed an oversize/overweight charge.

title: Fuel and flammable items prohibited in checked baggage
text: Any type of fuel is forbidden from transport in Checked Baggage in accordance with DOT Hazardous Materials Regulations.

title: Self-heating meals not permitted as carry-on or checked
text: Self-heating meals (i.e. MREs, flameless ration meals) are not permitted as Carry-On Baggage or Checked Baggage due to the risk of unintentional activation of the heating source.

title: Fishing rods must be checked if not stowable
text: Fishing poles that cannot be broken down adequately to be stowed on board in an overhead bin must be encased in a cylindrical fishing rod container acceptable to Alaska for withstanding normal Checked Baggage handling without sustaining damage to the rod and must be checked.
ambiguity_note: Container acceptability is determined by Alaska without stated criteria.

title: Golf equipment exceeding 62 inches exempt from oversize charge
text: Golf equipment exceeding 62 linear inches, may be checked without being assessed an oversize charge.

title: Hockey and lacrosse equipment exceeding 62 inches exempt from oversize charge
text: Hockey/Lacrosse equipment exceeding 62 linear inches, may be checked without being assessed an oversize/overweight charge.

title: Kayaks/Canoes checked baggage restrictions
text: Kayaks/Canoes are subject to standard overweight charges with maximum weight of 100 lbs./45 kg.

title: Kayaks/Canoes oversize exemption
text: Kayaks/Canoes exceeding 62 linear inches may be checked without being assessed an oversize charge.

title: Kayak construction and acceptance
text: Only kayaks of polyethylene construction are acceptable to Alaska. Kayaks of glass construction are not accepted. Kayaks are not accepted on Alaska flights operated by Horizon or SkyWest on behalf of Alaska Airlines.

title: Pole vaulting equipment acceptance
text: Pole vaulting equipment will be accepted on Alaska mainline flights only. It is not accepted on Alaska flights operated by Horizon or SkyWest on behalf of Alaska Airlines.

title: Pole vaulting equipment oversize exemption
text: Pole vaulting equipment exceeding 62 linear inches may be checked without being assessed an oversize charge.

title: Scuba tank at no additional charge
text: On flights operated solely by Alaska, Horizon, or SkyWest on behalf of Alaska, one scuba tank may be included as part of the scuba gear container and checked at no additional charge.

title: Scuba equipment oversize exemption
text: Scuba equipment exceeding 62 linear inches may be checked without being assessed an oversize charge.

title: Firearm case charges
text: Each individually checked firearm case is subject to standard Checked Baggage, overweight and/or oversize charges.

title: Firearm case size and weight limit
text: There is no limit to the number of items contained in a rifle, shotgun or pistol case, up to 50 lbs./23 kg., 62 linear inches maximum. Overweight or oversize items shall be subject to applicable charges.

title: Firearm packing requirements
text: Firearms must be unloaded and packed in (1) a manufacturer's crush-proof type container, manufactured specifically for the firearm or (2) a hard case acceptable to Alaska.
ambiguity_note: 'Hard case acceptable to Alaska' depends on Alaska's unstated discretion.

title: Minors may not transport firearms or ammunition
text: Minors under 18 may not transport a firearm(s)/ammunition.

title: Ammunition weight limits
text: Ammunition up to 50 lbs./23 kg. for domestic travel and up to 11 lbs./5 kg. for international travel is permitted on Alaska mainline flights and Horizon flights operated on behalf of Alaska Airlines only.

title: Firearms and ammunition not checked to foreign destinations via another carrier
text: Firearms and ammunition may not be checked to foreign destinations involving a Connection to another Carrier.

title: Skateboard baggage limit
text: A maximum of one skateboard if not in a case will be considered one piece of Checked Baggage. If in a proper case, there is no limit to the number of items as long as, it does not exceed 50 lbs./23 kg., 62 linear inches maximum.

title: Ski/snowboard equipment oversize exemption
text: Ski/snowboard equipment exceeding 62 linear inches may be checked without being assessed an oversize charge.

title: Surfboard oversize exemption
text: Surfboards/Paddleboards exceeding 62 linear inches may be checked without being assessed an oversize charge.

title: Kiteboarding oversize exemption
text: Kiteboarding equipment exceeding 62 linear inches may be checked without being assessed an oversize charge.

title: Football equipment charge
text: Each item will be subject to applicable baggage charge for a single piece, whether or not presented as a single piece.

title: Cabin-Seat Baggage charge
text: Alaska will charge 100% of the applicable Adult fare.

title: Cabin-Seat Baggage excluded from free allowance
text: Alaska will not include the Cabin-Seat Baggage in determination of free Baggage allowance or excess Baggage charges.

title: Cabin-Seat Baggage acceptance at Alaska discretion
text: Alaska determines in its sole and absolute discretion that the item is acceptable as Cabin-Seat Baggage but is so fragile and/or bulky as to require the use of a seat
ambiguity_note: Acceptance is decided at Alaska's sole discretion with no objective criteria stated.

title: Cabin-Seat Baggage weight limit
text: The weight of the item (including any case or covering) is not to impose any load on the aircraft's seats or floor structure that exceeds the load limitations for these components, and cannot exceed 165lbs./75 kg., or the applicable weight restrictions for the aircraft.

title: Cabin-Seat Baggage seat reservation and payment
text: A seat for ticketed Cabin-Seat Baggage must be reserved in advance and the applicable charges must be paid.

title: Cabin-Seat Baggage not in emergency exit seat
text: No Cabin-Seat Baggage may be secured in an emergency exit seat.

title: Cabin-Seat Baggage may be refused on some aircraft
text: Cabin-Seat Baggage may not be accepted on some aircraft with weight/size restrictions.
ambiguity_note: The aircraft types and size/weight restrictions are not specified.

title: International liability for baggage per passenger limit
text: the liability of Alaska is limited to 1,519 Special Drawing Rights ("SDRs") for each Passenger in the case of destruction, loss, damage, or delay of Baggage, whether checked or unchecked, under the Montreal Convention or the Warsaw Convention, whichever may apply.

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: Special declaration of interest for checked baggage
text: If a Passenger makes, at the time Checked Baggage is handed to Alaska, a special declaration of interest and has paid a supplementary sum, if applicable, Alaska will be liable for destruction, loss, damage, or delay of such Checked Baggage in an amount not exceeding the declared amount, unless Alaska proves that the declared amount is greater than the Passenger's actual interest in delivery at destination.
ambiguity_note: The supplementary sum and the maximum permissible declaration are not stated; the amount depends on Alaska's regulations.

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: Warsaw declared value threshold
text: In the case of transportation under the Warsaw Convention, no supplementary sum shall apply unless the declared amount exceeds 19 SDRs per kilogram of the total recorded weight of the Checked Baggage at the time the Baggage is handed to Alaska.

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: Warsaw deemed weight for lost or damaged baggage
text: the weight of each piece of such Baggage shall be deemed to be the maximum allowable weight for each piece of such Baggage under the applicable restrictions, unless the actual weight is stated on the Baggage Check.

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: Partial baggage delivery or damage proportional liability
text: the liability of Alaska with respect to the undelivered or damaged portion under the Warsaw Convention shall be reduced proportionately on the basis of weight, regardless of the value of any part of the Baggage or contents thereof.

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: No liability for baggage not in Alaska's charge
text: Alaska is not liable for destruction, loss, damage, or delay of Baggage not in the charge of Alaska, including Baggage undergoing security inspections or measures not under the control and direction of Alaska.

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: Checked baggage liability conditions and inherent defect exclusion
text: Alaska is liable for damage sustained in case of destruction or loss of Checked Baggage upon condition only that the event which caused the destruction or loss took place on board the aircraft or during any period within which the Checked Baggage was in the charge of Alaska. However, Alaska is not liable if and to the extent that the damage resulted from the inherent defect, quality or vice of the Baggage.

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: Defenses and limitations reserved
text: Alaska reserves all defenses and limitations available under the Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention, whichever may apply, to such claims

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: Limits not applicable in certain cases
text: The limits of liability shall not apply in cases described in Article 25 of the Warsaw Convention or Article 22 (5) of the Montreal Convention, whichever may apply.

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: Montreal and Warsaw rules supersede contract
text: the liability rules set out in the Montreal Convention and Warsaw Convention are fully incorporated by reference herein and shall supersede and prevail over any provisions of this Contract of Carriage which may be inconsistent with those rules.

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: Montreal Convention supersedes Rule 15 on interline liability
text: To the extent that the liability rules of the Montreal Convention conflict with Rule 15, the Montreal Convention shall supersede Rule 15.

provenance.section: Montreal Convention and the Warsaw Convention

title: Selecting Carrier checked baggage rules for Canada interline
text: The Selecting Carrier will: 1. Select and apply its own Baggage rules to the entire interline itinerary. OR 2. Select the Most Significant Carrier, as determined by IATA Resolution 302 and conditioned by the Canadian Transportation Agency, in order for that Carrier's Baggage rules, as established in its tariff, to apply to the entire Interline itinerary.

title: Carry-on baggage charges on interline itineraries
text: Notwithstanding, the Carry-On Baggage charges that will apply to the entire Interline itinerary will be those of the Selected Carrier.

title: Baggage rules applied by Participating Carrier
text: Where Alaska is not the Selected Carrier on an interline itinerary but is a Participating Carrier that is providing transportation to the Passenger based on the Ticket issued, Alaska will apply the Baggage rules of the Selected Carrier throughout the interline itinerary.

title: Domestic checked baggage liability cap
text: Maximum total liability of Alaska, if any, for substantiated damages in the event of loss, physical damage, or delay in the delivery of Checked Baggage, with the exception of wheelchairs, mobility aids, and Assistive Devices used by a Qualified Individual with a Disability, shall be limited to the proven amount of damage or loss, but in no event shall be greater than USD $4,700.00 per ticketed Passenger pursuant to 14 C.F.R. Section 254.4, unless the Passenger at time of check-in has declared the value of the Baggage to be in excess of USD $4,700.00 ("excess valuation") and has paid an additional charge for higher liability as provided below.

title: Compensation for reasonable documented baggage damages
text: Alaska will compensate the Passenger for reasonable, documented damages incurred as a direct result of the loss, damage to, or substantial delay in the delivery of such Baggage, up to the limit of liability, or declared value, whichever is higher, provided the Passenger has exercised reasonable efforts and good judgment to minimize the amount of damage.
ambiguity_note: 'Substantial delay' is not quantified in this clause.

title: Actual value of lost or damaged baggage
text: Actual value for reimbursement of lost or damaged property shall be determined by the documented original purchase price less depreciation for prior usage. Passenger will be responsible for documenting and proving the actual value of the loss.

title: Proof of claim for baggage expenses
text: For Baggage claims, reimbursement for any expenses will be based upon proof of claim acceptable to Alaska.
ambiguity_note: 'Proof of claim acceptable to Alaska' is not defined.

title: Lowest liability limit on combined carriers
text: When transportation is over the lines of Alaska and one or more Carriers with a limitation of liability other than USD $4,700.00 for each fare-paying Passenger and responsibility for the loss, damage or delay in delivery of Baggage cannot be determined, total liability of the combined Carriers will be the lowest maximum liability.

title: Wheelchair and assistive device liability (domestic)
text: Except for International Carriage to or from Canada, Alaska's maximum liability for a lost, damaged or destroyed wheelchair or other Assistive Device, is the original, documented purchased price of the device.

title: Game meat liability rate
text: Alaska will be liable for loss, but not damage or spoilage of "game meat" as Checked Baggage. Game meat includes any type of meat that was obtained by the Passenger by means other than purchasing in a store, for example: fresh caught fish or meat obtained from a hunt. Liability will be based on a flat rate of $10.00 per pound up to maximum liability of USD $4,700 per ticketed Passenger.

title: No liability where checked baggage undamaged, delayed or lost
text: Alaska does not assume liability for claims of missing or damaged items if a Passenger's Checked Baggage is not damaged, delayed, or lost.

title: Incidental damage excluded as normal wear
text: When Alaska has exercised ordinary standard of care, it assumes no liability for incidental damage such as scuffs, dents, stains, punctures, marks, dirt, scratches, and cuts that result from normal wear and tear.

title: Previously damaged items excluded
text: Alaska assumes no responsibility and will not be liable for further damage to previously damaged items. Alaska may, but is not obligated to, conditionally accept previously damaged items.
ambiguity_note: Acceptance of previously damaged items is discretionary and no conditions are specified.

title: Exclusion for protruding parts of checked baggage
text: Alaska shall not be liable for damage to protruding parts of Checked Baggage, including, but not limited to, wheels or feet, pockets, hanger hooks, pull handles, straps, zippers, locks, or telescoping handles that are attached to the exterior of Checked Baggage where such damage results from the inherent defect, quality or vice of the Checked Baggage.

title: Exclusion for manufacturing defects and fair wear
text: Furthermore, Alaska assumes no liability for defects in Baggage manufacture or for fair wear and tear resulting from ordinary handling of Checked Baggage. These exclusions apply whether or not the Passenger is advised by the customer service agent.

title: Carry-on baggage not covered unless Alaska at fault
text: Alaska will not be liable for damage, loss or theft of items taken on board an aircraft and remaining in the personal possession and care of the Passenger. Carry-On Baggage is the sole responsibility of the Passenger, and Alaska is liable only to the extent the damage resulted from its fault, or that of its contractors or agents.

title: Flight crew storage assistance does not shift liability
text: Assistance provided by flight crew members to properly store such items does not transfer liability to Alaska.

title: Unsuitable items excluded from checked baggage liability
text: The following items are judged to be unsuitable as contents of Checked Baggage. Except for certain International Carriage of such items subject to the terms of the Montreal Convention or Warsaw Convention, whichever may apply, Alaska assumes no liability for loss, theft, damage or delay in the delivery of: i. cash, currency; ii. negotiable papers; iii. securities; iv. business or personal contracts, documents; v. jewelry, watches; vi. cameras, videos and photographic equipment, camcorders, audio equipment, film, camera equipment, photographs; vii. electronic equipment/devices and personal electronic equipment/devices, including components thereof; viii. computers and related components; ix. binoculars, telescopes, optical devices including eyeglasses; x. silverware, pottery, porcelain and china; xi. precious metals, stones or materials; xii. art objects, sculptures, paintings; xiii. historical artifacts; xiv. original manuscripts; xv. irreplaceable books, publications, collectibles (such as baseball cards); xvi. antiques, heirlooms, collector's items, and artifacts; xvii. keys; xviii. sales samples and items intended for sale;

title: Excluded items in checked baggage
text: xxii. Note: When transportation is via Alaska and one or more Carriers which exclude certain items in Checked Baggage from their liability, Alaska will not be liable for the excluded items, except for certain International Carriage of such items subject to the terms of the Montreal Convention or Warsaw Convention, whichever may apply.
ambiguity_note: Refers to 'certain items' and 'certain International Carriage' without listing them here; the excluded items are defined elsewhere.

title: Attached items not liable
text: Alaska will not be liable for tents, sleeping bags, or similar articles which are strapped, taped, or tied to another piece of Baggage and may become separated as a result of normal handling during transportation.
ambiguity_note: 'Similar articles' is not defined.

title: Animals compliance and expenses
text: Passengers presenting animals for checking as Baggage or Carriage in the Passenger cabin will be responsible for compliance with all government regulations and restrictions, including furnishing valid health and vaccination certifications when required. Alaska will not be responsible for any expenses or loss that might result when any animal is refused passage into or through any country, state or territory.

title: Unclaimed baggage 30-minute limit
text: Alaska will not be liable for Baggage not claimed within 30 minutes after Baggage has been made available for claiming in a public Baggage claim area.

title: TSA lock damage exclusion
text: Alaska is not liable for locks damaged or missing as a result of TSA inspection.

title: Interline liability limits
text: When personal property, including Baggage, is tendered for transportation via Alaska in conjunction with another Carrier having a different limit of liability and/or declared higher value, Alaska shall not be liable for any amount in excess of its limits as specified herein.

title: Assistive device liability waiver
text: Alaska's normal limit of liability will be waived for substantiated claims involving loss, damage, or delay in delivery to wheelchairs or other Assistive Devices, when such items have been accepted into Alaska's care as Checked Baggage or otherwise.

title: Assistive device valuation basis
text: Except with respect to flights departing from the EEA or the UK, Alaska's liability for substantiated claims involving the loss of, damage to, or delay in delivery of wheelchairs or other Assistive Devices, when such items have been accepted as Checked Baggage or otherwise, is to be based on the cost of the repair or replacement value of the wheelchair or other Assistive Device.

title: Assistive device report within 24 hours
text: In the case of a lost, damaged, or destroyed wheelchair or other Assistive Device, the Passenger must make a written report to an Alaska representative within twenty-four (24) hours of arrival.

title: Assistive device report within 7 days for Canada
text: If the Passenger is unable to file a report within this timeframe, they must contact Alaska Central Baggage at 1-877-815-8253 (toll free within the U.S. and Canada) or here within seven (7) calendar days of arrival for Carriage to/from Canada.

title: Assistive device claim documentation
text: The Passenger must then complete a written claim form from Alaska within the time limitations defined in Rule 15.O above, if applicable, and provide documentary proof of loss or damage such as the baggage incident report number, the Passenger's itinerary, baggage tag, evidence of purchase, model, serial number and type of the wheelchair or other Assistive Device, and any other information that may be requested by Alaska to verify the facts alleged and to assess the credibility of the claim.
ambiguity_note: Says 'any other information that may be requested' and the time limit applies 'if applicable', leaving requirements open.

title: Assistive device repair option
text: If a wheelchair or other Assistive Device can be returned to the Passenger in the condition in which it was received by making reasonable repairs, Alaska may, at the Passenger's request, make the repairs.
ambiguity_note: Repair is at Alaska's discretion ('may') and conditional on the repair restoring original condition.

title: Assistive device refusal for size
text: Alaska reserves the right to refuse to transport large wheelchairs or other Assistive Devices that, due to the physical size of an aircraft compartment, cannot be carried upright safely without risk of serious damage to the wheelchair or Assistive Device, or that would cause a load imbalance in a small baggage compartment and violate weight and balance safety requirements.
ambiguity_note: 'Large' is not defined; refusal is discretionary.

title: Pre-existing damage inspection
text: Alaska has the right to inspect and document any pre-existing damage prior to acceptance of wheelchairs or other Assistive Devices as Checked Baggage.

title: Higher declared value maximum and charge
text: a Passenger may declare a value higher than the maximum amounts specified above, up to a maximum of USD $5,000.00 in which event Alaska's liability shall not exceed such higher declared value. The one-way charge for the declaration of higher value shall be USD $1.00 per USD $100.00 of additional declared value.

title: Excluded items not eligible for higher value
text: Excluded items listed in Rule 15(N)(1) above are not acceptable for higher value declaration.

title: Excess value coverage limited to checked point
text: Such Baggage must be checked, and excess valuation coverage will apply only to the point to which it is checked by Alaska and claimed by the Passenger.

title: Excess value charge at stopover
text: Excess value charges will be payable on a one-way basis at the point of origin for the entire journey to the final destination, provided that, if at a Stopover en route, a Passenger declares a higher excess value than that originally declared, additional value charges for the increased value from Stopover to the final destination will be due from the Passenger.

title: Excess value charge transfer exception
text: Excess value charges will be due from the Passenger to Alaska only to the point to which the Baggage is checked, or to the point of transfer to another Carrier, if such point is before the point to which Baggage is checked.

title: Discretion to refuse high-value baggage
text: Alaska has the discretion to not accept Baggage of any one Passenger having a declared value higher than $5,000 USD, unless special arrangements have been made in advance by the Passenger with Alaska.
ambiguity_note: Discretionary refusal; special arrangements are not defined.

title: Notice of baggage irregularity within 24 hours (domestic)
text: If all ticketed segments are for carriage within the U.S.A., the following applies: An incident involving loss of, or damage to, or delay in the delivery of Baggage or personal property accepted into the custody of Alaska must be reported in person or in writing to an Alaska representative within twenty-four (24) hours.

title: International claim presentment deadline
text: For International Carriage, no action shall be maintained for any loss of, or damage to, or any delay in the delivery of, any property or Baggage, or on any other claim (except claims for personal injury or death), arising out of or in connection with transportation of, or failure to transport any Passenger or property or Baggage unless the claim is presented in writing to an office of Alaska or its agent, or in the case of interline transportation, to the Carrier alleged to be responsible therefore immediately after the discovery or at the latest, within seven (7) days from the date of receipt of Checked Baggage.

title: International baggage delay claim deadline
text: In the case of delay, the complaint must be made at the latest within twenty-one (21) days from the date on which the Baggage has been returned; reimbursement will be based upon acceptable proof of claim.

title: Domestic claim notice deadline
text: For Domestic Carriage, notice and proof of loss must be presented in writing to an office of Alaska within forty-five (45) days after the alleged occurrence of the events giving rise to the claim, and any legal action arising from those events must be initiated within two (2 years).

title: Domestic notice sufficiency and good cause
text: Any written notification received within 45 days after which clearly indicates the nature of the claim is sufficient to meet the requirements for timely notice. Failure to give the above notice shall not be a bar if the claimant can show good cause for his/her failure to bring the claim within 45 days.
ambiguity_note: 'Good cause' is not defined; the two-year legal action period is missing a closing parenthesis and its unit is ambiguous.

title: Delayed baggage delivery charges conditions
text: Alaska will pay delayed Checked Baggage delivery charges only so long as such Baggage was tendered to Alaska by the Passenger in accordance with the minimum check-in times set forth in Section 15.C

title: Delayed baggage no guarantee of same flight
text: Where timely tender is made, Alaska will make reasonable efforts, but cannot guarantee, to transport such Baggage on the Passenger's flight(s), and Alaska will not assume responsibility for delivery charges if such Baggage arrives at the Passenger's destination on a subsequent flight.
ambiguity_note: Alaska makes only 'reasonable efforts' with no defined standard.

title: Disclosure of baggage rules at online purchase
text: when Alaska sells and issues a Ticket for an interline itinerary, it will disclose to the Passenger on any summary page at the end of an online purchase and on the Passenger’s itinerary/receipt and e-Ticket at the time of ticketing the Baggage information relevant to the Passenger itinerary as set out in paragraph (b) below. The disclosed information will reflect the Baggage rules of the Selected Carrier.

title: Refund of refund-restricted tickets when traveller does not travel through no fault of own
text: We will refund you as follows when we are the merchant of record (i) you refuse, or we refuse, to allow you to travel for reasons relating to Rule 13: Acceptance of Children, Rule 11: Refusal to Transport and Rule 8: Liability for Significantly Delayed or Changed Flights, Cancellations, and Denied Boarding and (ii) the reason for you not traveling is through no fault of your own. Any refund due will be made using the original form of payment.
ambiguity_note: 'through no fault of your own' is not defined in this chunk.

title: Refund of unused restricted ticket
text: If no portion of your Ticket has been used, you are entitled to a refund of an amount equal to the fare and fees applicable to the original Ticket issued to you.

title: Refund of partially used restricted ticket
text: If a portion of your Ticket has been used, you are entitled to a refund of an amount equal to the difference between (i) the fare and fees applicable to the original issued Ticket and (ii) the fare and fees applicable to the used portion of the Ticket.

title: Refundable ticket eligibility and surrender
text: For Tickets eligible for refund, upon your surrender of the unused or voided portion of a Ticket, we will refund you in accordance with the following terms and conditions: Any refund due will be made using the original form of payment.

title: Alaska-issued tickets only for refunds
text: Ticket must have been issued on Alaska Ticket Stock. The term “Alaska Ticket Stock” means Tickets which are identified with Alaska’s carrier code (027) as part of the Ticket serial number.

title: Refund of unused refundable ticket
text: If no portion of the Ticket has been used, the refund will be an amount equal to the fare and fees applicable to the original Ticket issued to you.

title: Refund of partially used refundable ticket
text: If a portion of the Ticket has been used, the refund will be an amount equal to the difference between (i) the fare and fees applicable to the original issued Ticket and (ii) the fare and fees applicable to the used portion of the Ticket.

title: Service fee on select international refunds
text: On select international routes a service fee may apply.
ambiguity_note: Fee applies only on 'select' routes and 'may apply'; routes and amount not specified.

title: Time limit for refund surrender
text: No refunds for any Tickets surrendered to us after 12 months of the original issue date of the Ticket.

title: Refund processing time
text: Upon meeting the above requirements, we will issue refunds for eligible Tickets within seven (7) business days for credit card purchases and twenty (20) business days for purchases made with cash, check, or other forms of payment.

title: Refund payee for ticket purchaser
text: We will make a refund in accordance with this Rule 17 to the purchaser of the Ticket except for purchases as made as follows:

title: Refund to credit card account
text: Tickets issued against a credit card: Refunds will, in principle, be processed through cancellation of the original credit card transaction. If such cancellation is not possible, the refund will be made to the account of the person whom such credit card has been issued.

title: Refund of travel agency-issued tickets
text: Tickets purchased through a travel agency or as part of a travel package: If a refund is authorized, the travel agency that issued the tickets will process the applicable refund to the ticketed customer.

title: Refund of upgrade fee on downgrade
text: If you are downgraded to a lower class of service, we will refund the upgrade fee you paid.

title: Refund of fare difference on first-class downgrade
text: If you paid for a first-class seat and were downgraded and elect to travel, we will refund you the difference between the fare you paid and the applicable Main Cabin fare if there is a fare difference.

title: Refund of baggage fees for lost or significantly delayed bags
text: If Alaska collected baggage fees for any of your checked bags and one or more of those bags are lost; or are delayed and the carrier that operated the last segment of the itinerary at your destination airport fails to reunite you with them within 12 hours (domestic travel) or 15/30 hours (international travel, depending on the length of the flight), of you being provided the opportunity to deplane after the last flight segment’s arrival (each such bag, a “Significantly Delayed Bag”), we will refund any fee charged and attributable to the lost or Significantly Delayed Bag, provided that you file a Mishandled Baggage Report (MBR).
ambiguity_note: International threshold is '15/30 hours depending on the length of the flight' without a stated rule for which applies.

title: Baggage fee refund when travel agent collected fees
text: If a travel agent collected the baggage fees, and we operated the last segment of your itinerary, we will refund any baggage fees for lost or Significantly Delayed Bags provided that you file an MBR.

title: Exclusions from baggage fee refunds
text: Alaska is not responsible for refunding any baggage fees for any Significantly Delayed Bag related to (i) any failure to pick-up and recheck your baggage at the first international entry point into the U.S., (ii) any failure to pick up your baggage where you are at fault, or (iii) your voluntary agreement to travel separately from your baggage.
ambiguity_note: 'where you are at fault' is not defined in this chunk.

title: No refund of baggage fees collected by another carrier
text: Alaska is also not responsible for refunding any baggage fees collected by another carrier.

title: Korea departure compensation standard
text: passengers departing from Korea are entitled to treatment and compensation in accordance with the Korea Fair Trade Commission’s Consumer Dispute Resolution Guidelines. Alaska Airlines may, under special circumstances, provide compensation exceeding those standards.
ambiguity_note: Discretionary 'may' and 'special circumstances' are undefined.

title: Involuntary refund of unused ticket
text: If no portion of the Ticket has been used and no portion of the transportation has been provided: An amount equal to the fare and charges paid.

title: Involuntary refund exception for unconfirmed unused tickets
text: Alaska shall not be obligated to refund any portion(s) of a fully unused Ticket which does not reflect a confirmed reservation on an Alaska flight involved in a schedule irregularity, unless such Ticket was issued by Alaska.

title: Involuntary refund of partially used ticket
text: If a portion of the Ticket has been used or a portion of the transportation has been provided, the refund will be equal to the difference, if any, between the fare and charges paid for the ticket, and the fare and charges applicable to the used portion of the Ticket.

title: No involuntary refund when alternative surface transport accepted
text: If alternative surface transportation is provided and is acceptable to the Passenger, no refund will be provided.
ambiguity_note: 'acceptable to the Passenger' has no objective test in this chunk.

title: Substitute service flight refund deferral
text: If fare is for transportation solely on substitute service flights involuntary refunds are deferred to the respective substitute service carrier's accounting office for computations.

title: No refund for co-terminal schedule irregularity transport
text: E. Alaska will make no refund if transportation is provided from the point of Schedule Irregularity to the ticketed destination or Stopover airport, or a co-terminal as determined by Alaska.
ambiguity_note: Co-terminal list is non-exhaustive ('include, but are not limited to') and determined by Alaska, leaving outcome to discretion.

title: EU261/UK261 refund where irregularity point does not serve final destination area
text: If the point of Scheduled Irregularity does not serve the same city, town or region of the final destination and you do not accept rebooking to your final destination you may choose a refund and transportation back to the airport of departure at the earliest convenience.

title: EU261/UK261 refund if co-terminal arrival exceeds 5 hours late
text: If the point of Scheduled Irregularity serves the same city, town or region (co-terminal) and we do not get you to your final destination within 5 hours of your originally scheduled arrival time, you may request a refund.
ambiguity_note: Passenger 'may request' a refund; the document does not state that Alaska must grant it.

title: Refund request time limitation
text: G. Time Limitation for Refund Requests: Refunds will not apply for Tickets presented later than one (1) year from the date of issuance of the original Ticket.

title: Voluntary refund conditions
text: the ticketed reservations is cancelled prior to the ticketed departure time, and (iii) the unused portion of the Alaska-issued ticket including the passenger receipt is surrendered.

title: Voluntary refund subject to fare rules and credit
text: Any refund will be subject to fare rules of the Ticket purchased. A Credit may be given for any Ticket that is refund-restricted according to its fare rules.
ambiguity_note: Uses 'may' for credit issuance; whether a credit is given is discretionary.

title: Taxes refundable only if fare refundable
text: Such taxes and charges are refundable only if the fare on which the tax or charge is assessed is itself refundable according to its fare rules.

title: Refund amount for unused ticket
text: If no portion of the Ticket has been used, the refund or Credit will be an amount equal to the fare, taxes, and charges paid.

title: Refund amount for partially used ticket
text: If a portion of the Ticket has been used, the refund or Credit will be an amount equal to the difference, if any, between the fare and charges paid for the Ticket, and the fare and charges applicable to the used portion of the Ticket.

title: Unused coupons surrender within one year
text: Refunds and Credits will be made in accordance with section 2 or section 3 provided that the unused flight coupons are surrendered to Alaska within one (1) year of the Ticket issue date.

title: No voluntary refund obligation for non-Alaska ticket stock
text: Alaska assumes no obligation to issue a voluntary refund unless such Ticket was issued on Alaska Ticket stock.

title: Bereavement refund for immediate family death
text: Alaska will issue a refund for a guest on a main fare who is unable to commence or continue travel because of the death of their immediate family member(s) (regardless of if they were traveling or not), or the guests traveling companion(s) traveling on the same itinerary and dates.

title: Compassion policy documentation requirements
text: Guests who meet the Compassion Policy criteria must provide the following information at the time of refund: name of deceased, relation of deceased to the passenger, name of the funeral home and phone number for the funeral home.

title: Credit form for Alaska-operated voluntary refunds
text: For Tickets on flights operated by Alaska, Horizon, and SkyWest, Alaska may issue a voluntary refund in the form of a Credit applicable only to flights operated by Alaska, Horizon, and SkyWest.
ambiguity_note: 'may' leaves the form of refund to Alaska's discretion.

title: Credit form for interline and codeshare voluntary refunds
text: for Tickets on Interline flights and flights operated by Codeshare Partners, Alaska may issue a voluntary refund in the form of a Credit applicable to Interline flights and flights operated by Codeshare Partners as well as flights operated by Alaska, Horizon, and SkyWest.
ambiguity_note: 'may' leaves the form of refund to Alaska's discretion.

title: Lost ticket refund application deadline
text: Application for refund of a lost Ticket must be made no later than one (1) month after the expiration date of the lost Ticket.

title: Lost ticket refund processing delay
text: Application must be made on forms prescribed by Alaska for such refunds, and refunds will not be issued earlier than four (4) months after receipt of proof of loss

title: Indemnity required for refund
text: Alaska will make such refund only provided that the person to whom refund is made agrees, in such forms as Alaska may require, to indemnify Alaska for any loss or damage which it may sustain by reason of such refund.

title: Refund location restriction
text: Alaska reserves the right to refuse to make any refund at a place other than that at which payment was made.
ambiguity_note: Discretionary right to refuse; no criteria stated.

title: Returned check service charge
text: Alaska will collect a service charge on any returned check of $25.00 USD/CAD, or the maximum permitted by applicable law, if less. This charge is nonrefundable and is not subject to any discount.

title: Nonrefundable fare not eligible for refund
text: The fare paid for unused travel by Passengers who purchase restricted, nonrefundable Tickets is not eligible for refunds, except as required by Applicable Laws.

title: Nonrefundable taxes and fees not refundable
text: Taxes, security fees, and Passenger Facility Charges associated with a nonrefundable fare are also not eligible for refund except as required by Applicable Laws.

title: Nonrefundable fare may convert to travel credit
text: The fare paid for unused travel by Passengers who purchase restricted, nonrefundable Tickets, including taxes, security fees, and Passenger Facility Charges, may be applied as travel Credit toward the purchase of future travel on Alaska, when requested directly with Alaska prior to scheduled departure time.

title: Shortfall paid by credit card
text: If the value of your BTC is insufficient to cover the full value of the ticket you wish to purchase, you may pay the difference with a credit card.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: Remaining BTC balance retained
text: If the ticket price is less than the value of the BTC, a credit balance will remain on the certificate until it is decreased to zero.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: No travel agency redemption
text: BTCs cannot be redeemed through a travel agency.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: Maximum four BTCs per reservation
text: Up to four BTCs can be applied on the billing page toward one reservation.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: Refund of unused ticket value as credit certificate
text: If a BTC is redeemed for a ticket and travel is not completed, the ticket value will be refunded as a credit certificate. The applicable fare rules will govern refunds and ticket exchanges.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)
ambiguity_note: Refund depends on applicable fare rules, which are not specified in this document.

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: BTC one-year validity
text: BTCs are valid for one year from issue date.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: Atmos Rewards accrual on BTC purchases
text: Atmos Rewards™ points may be accrued on tickets purchased with a BTC, subject to the Atmos Rewards conditions of membership.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)
ambiguity_note: Accrual is subject to external Atmos Rewards conditions not stated here.

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: BTC transferability and void if sold or bartered
text: BTCs are fully transferable, but will be void if bartered or sold.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: Cancellation or fare collection for bartered BTC
text: Alaska Airlines reserves the right to cancel reservations and/or collect the full fare for completed travel from the passenger or the original recipient of the BTC if they determine that the BTC has been bartered or sold.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)
ambiguity_note: Determination of bartering or sale is at airline discretion with no stated criteria.

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: BTC excluded from fees and certain purchases
text: BTCs cannot be applied to add/collect fees or used to purchase Alaska Airlines Vacations packages, air cargo services, services offered by Atmos Rewards hotel, cruise, or car rental partners.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: BTC excluded from Fly & Buy, trip protection and hotel/car
text: BTCs cannot be used to purchase Fly & Buy Points™, trip protection, or hotel and car reservations.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: BTC value in US dollars
text: The value of BTCs is in U.S. dollars.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: Risk of loss passes on transmission; no liability for lost or stolen BTC
text: The risk of loss and title for BTCs pass to the purchaser or transferee upon our electronic transmission to the recipient or transferee, whichever is applicable. Alaska Airlines is not responsible for lost or stolen BTCs.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: BTC void if altered or fraudulently obtained
text: BTCs are VOID if altered or obtained through illegal or fraudulent channels, or in a manner that violates the Atmos Rewards conditions of membership.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: Alternate payment for fraudulent BTC
text: Alaska Airlines reserves the right to request alternate forms of payment before permitting travel if a fraudulently or improperly obtained BTC is redeemed through alaskaair.com.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)
ambiguity_note: Right is discretionary ('reserves the right to request') with no stated criteria.

source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: No warranties on BTCs
text: ALASKA AIRLINES MAKES NO WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, WITH RESPECT TO BONUS TRAVEL CERTIFICATES, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION, ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

provenance.document_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)

title: Terms applicable to extent permitted by law

source_title: Bonus travel certificate terms (credit certificate behaviour)
